source.text: Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε, ἀδελφοί, γινώσκουσιν γὰρ νόμον λαλῶ, ὅτι ὁ νόμος κυριεύει τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ;

records.literal_gloss: Or are you ignorant, brothers, to those knowing for law I speak, that the law rules over the man for as long time [as] he lives?

en.L: Or do you not know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} (for I am speaking to those who know [the] law), that the law rules over a person for as long as [that person] lives?
en.B: Surely you understand, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, since I am speaking to people who know the law, that the law is master over someone only while that person is alive.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, you know about the law. So you know that the law has power over people only while they are alive.

es.L: ¿O no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}, hermanos (pues hablo a los que conocen [la] ley), que la ley tiene dominio sobre la persona mientras [esta] vive?
es.B: Sin duda {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}, hermanos, ya que hablo a personas que conocen la ley, que la ley es señora de alguien solo mientras esa persona vive.
es.R: Hermanos, {{plural_you:ustedes conocen|vosotros conocéis}} la ley. Por eso {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que la ley tiene poder sobre las personas solo mientras están vivas.

sw.L: Au hamjui, ndugu (kwa maana nasema na wale wanaoijua sheria), kwamba sheria inamtawala mtu kwa muda wote anaoishi?
sw.B: Hakika mnaelewa, ndugu, kwa kuwa nasema na watu wanaoijua sheria, kwamba sheria ina mamlaka juu ya mtu wakati tu mtu huyo yu hai.
sw.R: Ndugu, mnaijua sheria. Kwa hiyo mnajua kwamba sheria ina nguvu juu ya watu wakati tu wakiwa hai.

fr.L: Ou bien ignorez-vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} (car je parle à des gens qui connaissent [la] Loi), que la Loi exerce son autorité sur {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} aussi longtemps qu’il vit ?
fr.B: Vous le comprenez sûrement, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, puisque je parle à des gens qui connaissent la Loi : la Loi n’a autorité sur quelqu’un que tant qu’il est en vie.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, vous connaissez la Loi. Vous savez donc que la Loi a du pouvoir sur les gens seulement tant qu’ils sont vivants.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분은 알지 못합니까? 나는 율법을 아는 사람들에게 말하고 있습니다. 율법은 사람이 살아 있는 동안에만 그 사람을 지배한다는 것을 [모릅니까]?
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분도 잘 알 것입니다. 나는 율법을 아는 사람들에게 말하고 있으니 말입니다. 율법은 사람이 살아 있는 동안에만 그 사람의 주인 노릇을 합니다.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분은 율법을 알고 있습니다. 그러니 율법은 사람이 살아 있는 동안에만 그 사람에게 힘을 쓴다는 것도 알고 있습니다.

vi.L: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, hay là anh chị em không biết (vì tôi đang nói với những người biết luật pháp) rằng luật pháp làm chủ một người chừng nào người ấy còn sống?
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, chắc chắn anh chị em hiểu điều này, vì tôi đang nói với những người biết luật pháp: luật pháp chỉ làm chủ một người khi người ấy còn sống.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, anh chị em biết luật pháp. Vậy anh chị em biết rằng luật pháp chỉ có quyền trên con người khi họ còn sống.

pt.L: Ou vocês ignoram, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} (pois falo a quem conhece [a] Lei), que a Lei tem domínio sobre uma pessoa por todo o tempo em que [essa pessoa] vive?
pt.B: Vocês certamente entendem, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, já que falo a pessoas que conhecem a Lei, que a Lei é senhora de alguém só enquanto essa pessoa está viva.
pt.R: {{gender:Irmãos e irmãs|Irmãos}}, vocês conhecem a Lei. Então vocês sabem que a Lei tem poder sobre as pessoas só enquanto elas estão vivas.

am.L: ወይስ {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ሆይ፣ (ሕግን ለሚያውቁ እናገራለሁና) ሕግ ሰውን በሕይወት እስካለበት ጊዜ ድረስ እንደሚገዛው አታውቁምን?
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ሆይ፣ የምናገረው ሕግን ለሚያውቁ ሰዎች ስለ ሆነ፣ ሕግ በአንድ ሰው ላይ ጌታ የሚሆነው ያ ሰው በሕይወት እስካለ ድረስ ብቻ እንደ ሆነ በእርግጥ ታስተውላላችሁ።
am.R: {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ሆይ፣ ሕጉን ታውቃላችሁ። ስለዚህ ሕግ በሰዎች ላይ ሥልጣን የሚኖረው በሕይወት እስካሉ ድረስ ብቻ እንደ ሆነ ታውቃላችሁ።

ru.L: Или вы не знаете, {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}} (ведь я говорю знающим Закон), что Закон господствует над человеком, пока [тот] живёт?
ru.B: Вы ведь понимаете, {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}}, — я говорю с людьми, которые знают Закон, — что Закон властен над человеком только пока тот жив.
ru.R: {{gender:Братья и сёстры|Братья}}, вы знаете Закон. Поэтому вы знаете, что Закон имеет власть над людьми только пока они живы.

hi.L: या क्या तुम नहीं जानते, {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}} (क्योंकि मैं व्यवस्था के जाननेवालों से बात कर रहा हूँ), कि व्यवस्था मनुष्य पर तब तक प्रभुता करती है जब तक वह जीवित रहता है?
hi.B: {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, तुम तो समझते ही हो, क्योंकि मैं व्यवस्था जाननेवाले लोगों से बात कर रहा हूँ, कि व्यवस्था किसी पर केवल तब तक स्वामी रहती है जब तक वह व्यक्ति जीवित है।
hi.R: {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, तुम व्यवस्था के बारे में जानते हो। इसलिए तुम जानते हो कि व्यवस्था का लोगों पर अधिकार केवल तब तक रहता है जब तक वे जीवित हैं।

uk.L: Чи ви не знаєте, {{gender:брати і сестри|брати}} (бо я говорю до тих, хто знає Закон), що Закон панує над людиною, доки вона живе?
uk.B: Ви ж, певно, розумієте, {{gender:брати і сестри|брати}}, бо я говорю до людей, які знають Закон, що Закон панує над людиною лише доти, доки вона жива.
uk.R: {{gender:Брати і сестри|Брати}}, ви знаєте Закон. Тож ви знаєте, що Закон має владу над людьми тільки доти, доки вони живі.

ja.L: それとも、{{gender:きょうだいたち|兄弟たち}}――わたしは律法を知っている人々に話しているのですが――律法は人を、その人が生きている間支配する、ということを、あなたがたは知らないのですか？
ja.B: {{gender:きょうだいたち|兄弟たち}}、わたしは律法を知っている人々に話しているのですから、あなたがたにもわかるはずです。律法が人の主人であるのは、その人が生きている間だけです。
ja.R: {{gender:きょうだいたち|兄弟たち}}、みなさんは律法のことを知っています。ですから、律法が人に力をもつのは、その人が生きている間だけだということも、知っているはずです。

decisions.choice: Or: a new question that carries on from 6:14
alternatives: a fresh start with no link to chapter 6
decisions.reason: "Or" ties the chapter to what came before. In 6:14 Paul said that believers are "not under law but under grace"; now he shows from the law itself why its rule over them has ended.

decisions.choice: those who know the law: the law of Moses
alternatives: law in general, including Roman law
decisions.reason: Paul's readers in Rome, Jewish and Gentile believers alike, knew the Scriptures read in the synagogues, and the rest of the chapter is about the law of Moses (7:7). The word has no article, so some take it as law in general, a principle true of any legal system, Roman law included. The point is the same either way: law binds only the living.

decisions.choice: rules over: is master over
decisions.reason: kyrieuō is to be lord over someone. Paul used it in 6:9 (death no longer rules over Christ) and 6:14 (sin will not rule over you); now it is the law's rule that ends.

decisions.choice: the person lives, not the law
alternatives: as long as the law lives (is in force)
decisions.reason: The subject of "lives" is the person the law rules over. Grammatically it could be the law, but the illustration in verses 2-3 is about a person who dies.

decisions.choice: Surely you understand (B); you know (R)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes, we know", so Balanced and Readable say it as a statement. Literal keeps the question and the opening "Or".

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As through Romans: each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting, ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 1:13: "hermanos" already includes the sisters, so Spanish has no gender span on it in this chapter (here and 7:4).

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 1:13: "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili has no gender span in this chapter (here and 7:4).

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level, as in chapters 5-6
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Romans is a letter; even the "I" story of verses 7-11 is told as Paul's own account to his readers, so French uses the passé composé, with the imperfect for what went on.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in English and in Colossians: the church in Rome is addressed as men and women together, with "frères" as the traditional alternative.

decisions.choice: {{gender:l'être humain|l'homme}} (L); "quelqu'un" (B); "les gens" (R)
decisions.reason: French Literal needs a noun for the Greek "the man", meaning any person, and the gender setting goes on it; "il" that refers back to it agrees with either form. Balanced and Readable use "quelqu'un" and "les gens", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분", as settled at 1:13; "지배하다" (L) / "주인 노릇을 하다" (B) / "힘을 쓰다" (R) for the verb of 6:9, 6:14
decisions.reason: The address keeps the gender setting of the whole letter. The verb is the one used for sin and death as masters in chapter 6, so Literal keeps "지배하다" and Balanced keeps the picture of a master.

decisions.choice: Literal sets the parenthesis "나는 율법을 아는 사람들에게 말하고 있습니다" as its own sentence and repeats the question with "[모릅니까]"
decisions.reason: Korean cannot put a parenthesis inside a verb-final question without losing the reader; Literal keeps the Greek's order of thought by breaking the sentence and bracketing the repeated verb.

decisions.choice: the address "Thưa anh chị em" first (L)
alternatives: "Hay là anh chị em không biết, thưa anh chị em, ..."
decisions.reason: Vietnamese puts the respectful address at the head of the sentence; left in the middle, as in the Greek, it would follow "anh chị em" (you) and read as the same word twice.

decisions.choice: {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}
decisions.reason: As the English: Paul's "brothers" means the whole church in Rome, men and women, so the inclusive form is the default and the traditional "irmãos" the alternative (docs/portuguese-style.md section 7).

decisions.choice: a Lei é senhora de alguém
decisions.reason: "Lei" is feminine, so the English "master" becomes "senhora", which keeps the picture of a ruler from 6:9 and 6:14.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of this chapter
alternatives: capitalised pronouns for God and Christ, as the English alternative
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ in English (7:4) has nothing to change in Amharic.

decisions.choice: "ወንድሞችና እኅቶች ሆይ" with "ወንድሞች ሆይ" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Paul is addressing all the believers in Rome, women and men. The vocative "ሆይ" stands outside the span, since both options take it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}}
decisions.reason: As in 1:13: Paul writes to the whole church, women and men.

decisions.choice: {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the whole church, women and men, so the inclusive vocative is the default and "भाइयो" the alternative, as the style guide has it for adelphoi. The same in 7:4.

decisions.choice: the aside "for I am speaking to those who know the law" set off with "――" (L)
alternatives: moving the aside to the end as a separate sentence
decisions.reason: Japanese puts the main verb "知らないのですか" last, so the Greek aside would fall inside the question. Literal keeps it where Paul has it, between dashes; Balanced and Readable give it its own clause.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός.

records.literal_gloss: The for married woman to the living husband has been bound by law; if but should die the husband, she has been released from the law of the husband.

en.L: For the married woman is bound by law to the living husband; but if the husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband.
en.B: Take a married woman: the law binds her to her husband while he is alive. But if he dies, she is set free from the law that tied her to him.
en.R: For example, the law says that a married woman must stay with her husband while he is alive. But if her husband dies, that law no longer holds her.

es.L: Porque la mujer casada está ligada por ley al marido mientras él vive; pero si el marido muere, queda libre de la ley del marido.
es.B: Pensemos en una mujer casada: la ley la une a su marido mientras él está vivo. Pero si él muere, ella queda libre de la ley que la ataba a él.
es.R: Por ejemplo, la ley dice que una mujer casada debe permanecer con su esposo mientras él vive. Pero si su esposo muere, esa ley ya no la obliga.

sw.L: Kwa maana mwanamke aliyeolewa amefungwa kwa sheria na mume aliye hai; lakini mume akifa, amefunguliwa kutoka katika sheria ya mume.
sw.B: Chukua mfano wa mwanamke aliyeolewa: sheria inamfunga kwa mumewe wakati mume huyo yu hai. Lakini mume akifa, yeye anawekwa huru kutoka katika sheria iliyomfunga kwake.
sw.R: Kwa mfano, sheria inasema kwamba mwanamke aliyeolewa lazima akae na mumewe wakati mumewe yu hai. Lakini mumewe akifa, sheria hiyo haimfungi tena.

fr.L: Car la femme mariée est liée par [la] Loi au mari vivant ; mais si le mari meurt, elle est déliée de la loi du mari.
fr.B: Prenons une femme mariée : la Loi la lie à son mari tant qu’il est vivant. Mais s’il meurt, elle est libérée de la loi qui l’attachait à lui.
fr.R: Par exemple, la Loi dit qu’une femme mariée doit rester avec son mari tant qu’il est vivant. Mais si son mari meurt, cette loi ne la retient plus.

ko.L: 남편이 있는 여자는 남편이 살아 있는 동안에는 율법으로 그 남편에게 매여 있습니다. 그러나 남편이 죽으면, 그 여자는 남편의 법에서 풀려납니다.
ko.B: 예를 들어, 결혼한 여자는 남편이 살아 있는 동안에는 율법에 따라 남편에게 매여 있습니다. 그러나 남편이 죽으면, 그 여자를 남편에게 묶어 두던 법에서 풀려납니다.
ko.R: 예를 들어 봅시다. 율법에 따르면, 결혼한 여자는 남편이 살아 있는 동안에는 남편과 함께 살아야 합니다. 그러나 남편이 죽으면, 그 법은 더 이상 그 여자를 묶어 두지 못합니다.

vi.L: Vì người đàn bà có chồng bị luật pháp ràng buộc với người chồng đang sống; nhưng nếu người chồng chết, thì người vợ được giải thoát khỏi luật về người chồng.
vi.B: Chẳng hạn, một người phụ nữ có chồng bị luật pháp ràng buộc với chồng mình khi chồng còn sống. Nhưng nếu chồng chết, người vợ được giải thoát khỏi luật đã ràng buộc mình với chồng.
vi.R: Ví dụ, luật pháp nói rằng một người phụ nữ đã có chồng phải ở với chồng mình khi chồng còn sống. Nhưng nếu chồng chết, luật ấy không còn ràng buộc người ấy nữa.

pt.L: Pois a mulher casada está ligada pela lei ao marido vivo; mas, se o marido morrer, ela fica livre da lei do marido.
pt.B: Vejam a mulher casada: a lei a prende ao marido enquanto ele está vivo. Mas, se ele morrer, ela fica livre da lei que a ligava a ele.
pt.R: Por exemplo, a lei diz que uma mulher casada deve ficar com o marido enquanto ele estiver vivo. Mas, se o marido morrer, essa lei não a prende mais.

am.L: ምክንያቱም ባል ያላት ሴት በሕይወት ላለው ባሏ በሕግ ታስራለች፤ ባሏ ቢሞት ግን ከባል ሕግ ተፈትታለች።
am.B: ያገባችን ሴት እንደ ምሳሌ ውሰዱ፤ ባሏ በሕይወት እያለ ሕግ ከእርሱ ጋር ያስራታል። ባሏ ቢሞት ግን ከእርሱ ጋር ካስተሳሰራት ሕግ ነጻ ትሆናለች።
am.R: ለምሳሌ ያገባች ሴት ባሏ በሕይወት እስካለ ድረስ ከእርሱ ጋር መኖር እንዳለባት ሕጉ ይናገራል። ባሏ ቢሞት ግን ያ ሕግ ከእንግዲህ አያስራትም።

ru.L: Ведь замужняя женщина законом привязана к живому мужу; если же муж умрёт, она освобождается от закона мужа.
ru.B: Возьмём замужнюю женщину: закон связывает её с мужем, пока он жив. Но если он умрёт, она свободна от закона, который связывал её с ним.
ru.R: Например, закон говорит, что замужняя женщина должна оставаться со своим мужем, пока он жив. Но если её муж умрёт, этот закон больше её не держит.

hi.L: क्योंकि विवाहित स्त्री व्यवस्था के द्वारा जीवित पति से बंधी है; पर यदि पति मर जाए, तो वह पति की व्यवस्था से छूट जाती है।
hi.B: एक विवाहित स्त्री को ही लो: जब तक उसका पति जीवित है, व्यवस्था उसे पति से बाँधे रखती है। पर यदि वह मर जाए, तो वह उस व्यवस्था से छूट जाती है जो उसे पति से बाँधती थी।
hi.R: उदाहरण के लिए, व्यवस्था कहती है कि एक विवाहित स्त्री को अपने पति के जीवित रहते उसके साथ रहना है। पर यदि उसका पति मर जाए, तो वह व्यवस्था उस पर लागू नहीं रहती।

uk.L: Бо заміжня жінка Законом привʼязана до живого чоловіка; а якщо чоловік помре, вона звільнена від Закону про чоловіка.
uk.B: Візьмімо заміжню жінку: Закон привʼязує її до чоловіка, поки він живий. Але якщо він помре, вона звільняється від Закону, що вʼязав її з ним.
uk.R: Наприклад, Закон каже, що заміжня жінка мусить залишатися з чоловіком, поки він живий. Але якщо її чоловік помре, цей Закон більше її не тримає.

ja.L: というのは、夫のある女は、生きている夫に律法によって結ばれています。しかし、夫が死ねば、夫の律法から解かれているのです。
ja.B: たとえば、結婚している女性は、夫が生きている間は、律法によって夫に結ばれています。しかし夫が死ねば、夫と自分を結んでいた律法から解き放たれます。
ja.R: たとえば、律法によれば、結婚している女の人は、夫が生きている間は夫と共にいなければなりません。けれども夫が死ねば、その律法にはもうしばられません。

decisions.choice: a married woman bound to her husband by the law
decisions.reason: hypandros means "under a husband", that is, married. Under the law of Moses a wife was bound to her husband, and it was the husband who could end the marriage (Deuteronomy 24:1-4); only his death set her free without question.

decisions.choice: released: the law no longer has any claim on her
decisions.reason: katargeō means to make ineffective or to release. The perfect tense says she stays released. Paul uses the same verb of believers in verse 6: "we have been released from the law".

decisions.choice: the law of the husband: the law that binds her to her husband
decisions.reason: The genitive means the law as it concerns the husband, the marriage law, not a law that the husband made.

decisions.choice: Take a married woman (B); For example (R)
decisions.reason: "For" introduces an illustration of verse 1. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "la loi du mari" in lower case
decisions.reason: The phrase means the part of the law that binds a wife to her husband, the marriage law, so it is written in lower case; the law of Moses as a whole keeps its capital.

decisions.choice: "남편의 법" (L); "남편에게 묶어 두던 법" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "the law of the husband" as the law that binds her to him. Literal keeps the short phrase; Balanced and Readable say what it means. "법" rather than "율법" because the phrase names one part of the law.

decisions.choice: "luật về người chồng" (L); "luật đã ràng buộc mình với chồng" (B)
decisions.reason: The phrase means the law that binds her to her husband (m3). "Luật pháp của người chồng" would sound like a law the husband owns or makes, so Vietnamese says what the law is about.

decisions.choice: a lei (lowercase) in verses 2-3
decisions.reason: In the illustration "lei" is the marriage law as it concerns the husband (m3), so it takes a small letter; "a Lei" with a capital is kept for the Law of Moses as a whole (verses 1, 4-9).

decisions.choice: "解かれている" (L); "解き放たれる" (B)
decisions.reason: katargeō here means the law no longer has any claim on her (m2). The same Japanese verb is used for believers in verse 6 ("律法から解かれました" / "解き放たれています"), so the reader can see Paul's link.

source.text: ἄρα οὖν ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, τοῦ μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν μοιχαλίδα γενομένην ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ.

records.literal_gloss: So then, being alive the husband, an adulteress she will be called if she becomes to another man; if but should die the husband, free she is from the law, so that not to be her an adulteress having become to another man.

en.L: So then, while the husband is alive, she will be called an adulteress if she becomes another man's; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress if she becomes another man's.
en.B: So if she joins herself to another man while her husband is still living, people will call her an adulteress. But once her husband has died she is free from the law, and marrying another man does not make her an adulteress.
en.R: So if she marries another man while her husband is still alive, she is guilty of adultery. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law. Then she can marry another man, and it is not adultery.

es.L: Así que, mientras vive el marido, será llamada adúltera si llega a ser de otro hombre; pero si el marido muere, es libre de la ley, de modo que no es adúltera si llega a ser de otro hombre.
es.B: Por eso, si se une a otro hombre mientras su marido aún vive, la llamarán adúltera. Pero una vez que su marido ha muerto, es libre de la ley, y casarse con otro hombre no la hace adúltera.
es.R: Así que, si se casa con otro hombre mientras su esposo todavía vive, comete adulterio. Pero si su esposo muere, queda libre de esa ley. Entonces puede casarse con otro hombre, y no es adulterio.

sw.L: Basi, mume akiwa hai, ataitwa mzinzi kama akiwa wa mwanamume mwingine; lakini mume akifa, yu huru kutoka katika sheria, hata asiwe mzinzi akiwa wa mwanamume mwingine.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, akijiunga na mwanamume mwingine wakati mumewe bado yu hai, watu watamwita mzinzi. Lakini mumewe akishakufa, yu huru kutoka katika sheria, na kuolewa na mwanamume mwingine hakumfanyi kuwa mzinzi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, akiolewa na mwanamume mwingine wakati mumewe bado yu hai, ana hatia ya uzinzi. Lakini mumewe akifa, yu huru kutoka katika sheria hiyo. Hapo anaweza kuolewa na mwanamume mwingine, na huo si uzinzi.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, du vivant du mari, elle sera appelée adultère si elle devient [la femme] d’un autre homme ; mais si le mari meurt, elle est libre à l’égard de la loi, de sorte qu’elle n’est pas adultère si elle devient [la femme] d’un autre homme.
fr.B: Si donc elle s’unit à un autre homme du vivant de son mari, on l’appellera adultère. Mais une fois son mari mort, elle est libre à l’égard de la loi, et épouser un autre homme ne fait pas d’elle une adultère.
fr.R: Donc, si elle épouse un autre homme alors que son mari est encore vivant, elle commet un adultère. Mais si son mari meurt, elle est libre par rapport à cette loi. Alors elle peut épouser un autre homme, et ce n’est pas un adultère.

ko.L: 그러므로 남편이 살아 있는 동안에 그 여자가 다른 남자의 [사람이] 되면 간음한 여자라고 불릴 것입니다. 그러나 남편이 죽으면 그 여자는 그 법에서 자유로우므로, 다른 남자의 [사람이] 되어도 간음한 여자가 되지 않습니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 남편이 살아 있는데 다른 남자와 함께 살면, 사람들은 그 여자를 간음한 여자라고 부를 것입니다. 그러나 남편이 죽으면 그 여자는 그 법에서 자유로워져서, 다른 남자와 결혼해도 간음한 여자가 되지 않습니다.
ko.R: 그래서 남편이 아직 살아 있는데 다른 남자와 결혼하면, 그 여자는 간음죄를 짓는 것입니다. 그러나 남편이 죽으면 그 여자는 그 법에서 자유롭습니다. 그때는 다른 남자와 결혼해도 간음이 아닙니다.

vi.L: Vậy thì, khi người chồng còn sống, nếu người vợ thuộc về một người đàn ông khác, thì sẽ bị gọi là người đàn bà ngoại tình; nhưng nếu người chồng chết, người vợ được tự do khỏi luật pháp, đến nỗi không phải là người đàn bà ngoại tình khi thuộc về một người đàn ông khác.
vi.B: Vì thế, nếu người vợ đi theo một người đàn ông khác khi chồng còn sống, người ta sẽ gọi người ấy là kẻ ngoại tình. Nhưng nếu chồng đã chết, người vợ được tự do khỏi luật pháp, và việc lấy một người đàn ông khác không khiến người ấy thành kẻ ngoại tình.
vi.R: Vậy nếu người vợ lấy một người đàn ông khác khi chồng còn sống, thì người ấy phạm tội ngoại tình. Nhưng nếu chồng chết, người ấy được tự do khỏi luật đó. Khi ấy người ấy có thể lấy một người đàn ông khác, và đó không phải là ngoại tình.

pt.L: Assim, então, enquanto o marido vive, ela será chamada adúltera se ela se tornar de outro homem; mas, se o marido morrer, ela está livre da lei, de modo que não é adúltera se se tornar de outro homem.
pt.B: Assim, se ela se unir a outro homem enquanto o marido ainda vive, será chamada de adúltera. Mas, depois que o marido morre, ela está livre da lei, e casar com outro homem não faz dela uma adúltera.
pt.R: Então, se ela se casar com outro homem enquanto o marido ainda está vivo, ela comete adultério. Mas, se o marido morrer, ela está livre dessa lei. Aí ela pode se casar com outro homem, e isso não é adultério.

am.L: ስለዚህ እንግዲህ ባሏ በሕይወት እያለ ለሌላ ወንድ ብትሆን አመንዝራ ትባላለች፤ ባሏ ቢሞት ግን ከሕጉ ነጻ ናት፤ ስለዚህ ለሌላ ወንድ ብትሆን አመንዝራ አይደለችም።
am.B: ስለዚህ ባሏ ገና በሕይወት እያለ ከሌላ ወንድ ጋር ብትሆን ሰዎች አመንዝራ ይሏታል። ባሏ ከሞተ በኋላ ግን ከሕጉ ነጻ ናት፤ ሌላ ወንድ ብታገባም አመንዝራ አያደርጋትም።
am.R: ስለዚህ ባሏ ገና በሕይወት እያለ ሌላ ወንድ ብታገባ ምንዝር ፈጽማለች። ባሏ ቢሞት ግን ከዚያ ሕግ ነጻ ናት። ከዚያም ሌላ ወንድ ማግባት ትችላለች፤ ይህም ምንዝር አይደለም።

ru.L: Итак, при живом муже она будет названа прелюбодейкой, если станет [женой] другого мужчины; если же муж умрёт, она свободна от закона, так что не будет прелюбодейкой, став [женой] другого мужчины.
ru.B: Поэтому если при живом муже она соединится с другим мужчиной, её назовут прелюбодейкой. Но когда её муж умер, она свободна от закона, и выйти замуж за другого не делает её прелюбодейкой.
ru.R: Поэтому если она выйдет замуж за другого мужчину, пока её муж ещё жив, она виновна в измене. Но если её муж умрёт, она свободна от этого закона. Тогда она может выйти замуж за другого, и это не измена.

hi.L: इसलिए यदि पति के जीते जी वह किसी दूसरे पुरुष की हो जाए, तो व्यभिचारिणी कहलाएगी; पर यदि पति मर जाए, तो वह उस व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र है, यहाँ तक कि यदि वह किसी दूसरे पुरुष की हो जाए, तो भी व्यभिचारिणी नहीं।
hi.B: इसलिए यदि पति के जीवित रहते वह किसी दूसरे पुरुष के साथ जुड़ जाए, तो लोग उसे व्यभिचारिणी कहेंगे। पर जब उसका पति मर गया, तो वह व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र है, और किसी दूसरे पुरुष से विवाह करने से वह व्यभिचारिणी नहीं बनती।
hi.R: इसलिए यदि वह अपने पति के जीवित रहते किसी दूसरे पुरुष से विवाह करे, तो वह व्यभिचार की दोषी है। पर यदि उसका पति मर जाए, तो वह उस व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र है। तब वह किसी दूसरे पुरुष से विवाह कर सकती है, और यह व्यभिचार नहीं है।

uk.L: Тож за життя чоловіка вона називатиметься перелюбницею, якщо стане [дружиною] іншого чоловіка; а якщо чоловік помре, вона вільна від Закону, так що не буде перелюбницею, ставши [дружиною] іншого чоловіка.
uk.B: Тож якщо вона зійдеться з іншим чоловіком, поки її чоловік живий, її назвуть перелюбницею. Але коли її чоловік помер, вона вільна від Закону, і шлюб з іншим чоловіком не робить її перелюбницею.
uk.R: Тож якщо вона вийде заміж за іншого, поки її чоловік ще живий, вона винна в перелюбі. Але якщо її чоловік помре, вона вільна від цього Закону. Тоді вона може вийти заміж за іншого, і це не перелюб.

ja.L: ですから、夫が生きているうちに、ほかの男のものとなるなら、彼女は姦淫の女と呼ばれることになります。しかし、夫が死ねば、彼女は律法から自由であって、ほかの男のものとなっても、姦淫の女とはなりません。
ja.B: ですから、夫がまだ生きているのにほかの男と一緒になれば、彼女は人々から姦淫の女と呼ばれます。しかし夫が死んだなら、彼女は律法から自由であり、ほかの男と結婚しても姦淫の女にはなりません。
ja.R: ですから、夫がまだ生きているのにほかの男の人と結婚すれば、その女の人は姦淫の罪を犯すことになります。しかし夫が死ねば、その律法から自由になります。そして、ほかの男の人と結婚しても、姦淫にはなりません。

decisions.choice: become another man's: marry or live as his wife
decisions.reason: "To become to a man" is a Greek way, taken from the Greek Old Testament, of saying a woman is joined to a man as his wife (Deuteronomy 24:2). Paul uses the same words of believers in verse 4: they now belong to another.

decisions.choice: she will be called: she will bear the name publicly
decisions.reason: chrēmatizō here means to be known by a name. The point is how the law and the community would judge her.

decisions.choice: so that she is not an adulteress: the result of her freedom
decisions.reason: The infinitive clause gives the result of being free from the law: a second marriage after her husband's death is not adultery.

decisions.choice: joins herself to / marrying (B); marries (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "becomes another man's" means (m1). Literal keeps the Greek expression so that the link with verse 4 can be seen.

decisions.choice: "다른 남자의 [사람이] 되다" (L); "다른 남자와 함께 살다 / 결혼하다" (B); "결혼하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom "become another man's" means to marry or live as his wife (meaning decision). Literal keeps it with a bracket; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

decisions.choice: "thuộc về một người đàn ông khác" (L); "đi theo", "lấy" (B); "lấy" (R)
decisions.reason: "Become another man's" means to marry him or live as his wife (m1). Literal keeps the idea of belonging, which Paul takes up in verse 4; Balanced and Readable say it with the plain words for going with or marrying a man.

decisions.choice: "ほかの男のものとなる" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek idiom "become another man's" (m1), because verse 4 uses the same words of believers who now belong to the risen Christ ("ほかの方のものとなり").

source.text: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐθανατώθητε τῷ νόμῳ διὰ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι ὑμᾶς ἑτέρῳ, τῷ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθέντι ἵνα καρποφορήσωμεν τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: So, brothers of me, also you were put to death to the law through the body of the Christ, for the to become you to another, to the [one] from dead [ones] having been raised, so that we may bear fruit to God.

en.L: So then, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you also were put to death to the law through the body of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, for you to become another's, [belonging] to the one raised from [the] dead, so that we might bear fruit for God.
en.B: It is the same with you, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Through the body of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} you were put to death as far as the law is concerned, so that you could be joined to another: to the one who was raised from the dead. And so we can bear fruit for God.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, it is the same with you. When {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died on the cross, you died with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the law lost its hold on you. Now you belong to someone else, to the one who was raised from death. So now our lives can produce good things for God.

es.L: Así que, hermanos míos, también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se {{plural_you:les|os}} dio muerte a la ley por medio del cuerpo {{christos:del Cristo|del Mesías}}, para que {{plural_you:pertenezcan|pertenezcáis}} a otro, al que fue resucitado de [los] muertos, a fin de que llevemos fruto para Dios.
es.B: Lo mismo pasa con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos míos. Por medio del cuerpo {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se {{plural_you:les|os}} dio muerte en lo que respecta a la ley, para que {{plural_you:pudieran unirse|pudierais uniros}} a otro: al que fue resucitado de entre los muertos. Y así podemos dar fruto para Dios.
es.R: Hermanos míos, lo mismo pasa con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Cuando {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió en la cruz, {{plural_you:ustedes murieron|vosotros moristeis}} con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y la ley perdió su poder sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Ahora {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} a otro, al que resucitó de la muerte. Así, nuestra vida puede producir cosas buenas para Dios.

sw.L: Basi, ndugu zangu, ninyi pia mliuawa kwa habari ya sheria kupitia mwili wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ili mpate kuwa wa mwingine, wa yule aliyefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, ili tumzalie Mungu matunda.
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo kwenu pia, ndugu zangu. Kupitia mwili wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ninyi mliuawa kwa upande wa sheria, ili muweze kuunganishwa na mwingine, yaani yule aliyefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu. Na hivyo tunaweza kumzalia Mungu matunda.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, ndivyo ilivyo kwenu pia. {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alipokufa msalabani, ninyi mlikufa pamoja naye, na sheria ikapoteza nguvu zake juu yenu. Sasa ninyi ni mali ya mwingine, wa yule aliyefufuka kutoka kwa wafu. Kwa hiyo sasa maisha yetu yanaweza kumzalia Mungu mambo mema.

fr.L: Ainsi, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous aussi, vous avez été mis à mort à l’égard de la Loi par le corps du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, pour que vous deveniez [ceux] d’un autre, de celui qui a été ressuscité d’entre [les] morts, afin que nous portions du fruit pour Dieu.
fr.B: Il en est de même pour vous, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Par le corps du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, vous avez été mis à mort pour ce qui est de la Loi, afin de pouvoir être unis à un autre : à celui qui a été ressuscité d’entre les morts. Et ainsi, nous pouvons porter du fruit pour Dieu.
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, c’est la même chose pour vous. Quand le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort sur la croix, vous êtes morts avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et la Loi a perdu son pouvoir sur vous. Maintenant, vous appartenez à quelqu’un d’autre, à celui qui a été ramené de la mort à la vie. Alors maintenant, notre vie peut produire de bonnes choses pour Dieu.

ko.L: 그러므로 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분도 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 몸을 통하여 율법에 대하여 죽임을 당했습니다. 이는 여러분이 다른 분, 곧 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나신 분의 [사람이] 되어, 우리가 하나님께 열매를 맺게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분도 마찬가지입니다. 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 몸을 통해 율법에 대해서는 죽임을 당했습니다. 그것은 여러분이 다른 분, 곧 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나신 분께 속하게 하려는 것입니다. 그리하여 우리는 하나님을 위해 열매를 맺게 되었습니다.
ko.R: 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분도 마찬가지입니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 십자가에서 죽으셨을 때, 여러분도 그분과 함께 죽었습니다. 그래서 율법은 더 이상 여러분을 붙잡아 둘 수 없습니다. 이제 여러분은 다른 분, 곧 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나신 분께 속해 있습니다. 그래서 이제 우리의 삶은 하나님을 위해 좋은 열매를 맺을 수 있습니다.

vi.L: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, anh chị em cũng đã được làm cho chết đối với luật pháp qua thân thể của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, để anh chị em thuộc về một người khác, [tức là] Đấng đã được sống lại từ kẻ chết, để chúng ta sinh bông trái cho Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, anh chị em cũng vậy. Qua thân thể của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, anh chị em đã được làm cho chết đối với luật pháp, để anh chị em được kết hợp với một người khác, là Đấng đã được sống lại từ cõi chết. Nhờ vậy chúng ta có thể sinh bông trái cho Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, anh chị em cũng vậy. Khi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} chết trên thập tự giá, anh chị em đã chết với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và luật pháp không còn nắm giữ anh chị em nữa. Bây giờ anh chị em thuộc về một người khác, là Đấng đã được sống lại từ cõi chết. Vì vậy, giờ đây đời sống chúng ta có thể sinh ra những điều tốt đẹp cho Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: Assim, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, também vocês foram mortos para a Lei por meio do corpo do {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, para vocês se tornarem de outro, daquele que foi ressuscitado dentre [os] mortos, a fim de que demos fruto para Deus.
pt.B: O mesmo acontece com vocês, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}. Por meio do corpo {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}}, vocês morreram no que diz respeito à Lei, para que pudessem pertencer a outro: àquele que foi ressuscitado dentre os mortos. E assim podemos dar fruto para Deus.
pt.R: Meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, com vocês acontece o mesmo. Quando {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} morreu na cruz, vocês morreram com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, e a Lei perdeu o poder sobre vocês. Agora vocês pertencem a outro, àquele que foi ressuscitado dentre os mortos. Por isso a nossa vida pode produzir coisas boas para Deus.

am.L: ስለዚህ {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ እናንተ ደግሞ {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} አካል በኩል ለሕግ ተገድላችኋል፤ ይኸውም የሌላው፣ ከሙታን የተነሣው [የእርሱ] እንድትሆኑ፣ ለእግዚአብሔርም ፍሬ እንድናፈራ ነው።
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ እናንተም እንደዚሁ ናችሁ። የሌላው፣ ከሙታን የተነሣው እንድትሆኑ {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} አካል በኩል ከሕግ አንጻር ተገድላችኋል። በዚህም ለእግዚአብሔር ፍሬ ማፍራት እንችላለን።
am.R: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ እናንተም እንደዚሁ ናችሁ። {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በመስቀል ላይ በሞተ ጊዜ እናንተም ከእርሱ ጋር ሞታችሁ፤ ሕጉም በእናንተ ላይ የነበረውን ሥልጣን አጣ። አሁን የሌላው፣ ከሞት የተነሣው ናችሁ። ስለዚህ አሁን ሕይወታችን ለእግዚአብሔር መልካም ፍሬ ማፍራት ይችላል።

ru.L: Так и вы, {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}} мои, умерщвлены для Закона через тело {{christos:Христа|Мессии}}, чтобы вам принадлежать другому, Воскрешённому из мёртвых, чтобы мы приносили плод Богу.
ru.B: Так и с вами, мои {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}}. Через тело {{christos:Христа|Мессии}} вы умерли для Закона, чтобы принадлежать другому — тому, кто воскрешён из мёртвых. И так мы можем приносить плод Богу.
ru.R: Мои {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}}, так и с вами. Когда {{christos:Христос|Мессия}} умер на кресте, вы умерли вместе с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, и Закон потерял над вами власть. Теперь вы принадлежите другому — тому, кто воскрешён из мёртвых. Так теперь наша жизнь может приносить Богу добрые плоды.

hi.L: इसलिए, हे मेरे {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, तुम भी मसीह की देह के द्वारा व्यवस्था के लिए मार डाले गए, कि तुम दूसरे के हो जाओ, अर्थात् उनके जो मरे हुओं में से जिलाए गए, ताकि हम परमेश्वर के लिए फल लाएँ।
hi.B: मेरे {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, तुम्हारे साथ भी ऐसा ही है। मसीह की देह के द्वारा तुम व्यवस्था के लिए मार डाले गए, ताकि तुम किसी दूसरे से जुड़ जाओ: उनसे जो मरे हुओं में से जिलाए गए। और इस प्रकार हम परमेश्वर के लिए फल ला सकते हैं।
hi.R: मेरे {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, तुम्हारे साथ भी ऐसा ही है। जब मसीह क्रूस पर मरे, तो तुम भी उनके साथ मर गए, और व्यवस्था की तुम पर पकड़ नहीं रही। अब तुम किसी और के हो, उनके जो मृत्यु से जिलाए गए। इसलिए अब हमारा जीवन परमेश्वर के लिए अच्छे फल ला सकता है।

uk.L: Тож, мої {{gender:брати і сестри|брати}}, і ви були умертвлені для Закону через тіло {{christos:Христа|Месії}}, щоб вам належати іншому — тому, хто воскрешений із мертвих, — щоб ми приносили плід Богові.
uk.B: Так і з вами, мої {{gender:брати і сестри|брати}}. Через тіло {{christos:Христа|Месії}} ви вмерли для Закону, щоб належати іншому — тому, хто воскрес із мертвих. І так ми можемо приносити плід Богові.
uk.R: Мої {{gender:брати і сестри|брати}}, так само і з вами. Коли {{christos:Христос|Месія}} помер на хресті, ви померли разом з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, і Закон утратив над вами владу. Тепер ви належите іншому — тому, хто воскрес із мертвих. Тож тепер наше життя може приносити Богові добрі плоди.

ja.L: こうして、わたしの{{gender:きょうだいたち|兄弟たち}}、あなたがたも、{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}の体を通して、律法に対して死なされました。それは、あなたがたがほかの方のもの、すなわち死者たちの中から起こされた方のものとなり、わたしたちが神のために実を結ぶためです。
ja.B: わたしの{{gender:きょうだいたち|兄弟たち}}、あなたがたも同じです。{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}の体を通して、あなたがたは律法に関しては死んだ者とされました。それは、ほかの方、すなわち死者の中からよみがえらされた方に結ばれるためです。こうしてわたしたちは、神のために実を結ぶことができるのです。
ja.R: わたしの{{gender:きょうだいたち|兄弟たち}}、みなさんも同じです。{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}が十字架の上で死なれたとき、みなさんもその方と共に死に、律法はみなさんをしばる力を失いました。今、みなさんはほかの方、つまり死者の中からよみがえらされた方のものです。ですから今、わたしたちは、神のために良い実を結ぶ生き方ができるのです。

decisions.choice: So then: the point of the illustration
decisions.reason: Paul applies verses 2-3. The picture does not match at every point (there the husband dies, here believers die), but the point holds: a death ends the law's claim and leaves a person free to belong to another.

decisions.choice: through the body of Christ: through his death on the cross, which believers share
alternatives: through belonging to the church, Christ's body
decisions.reason: Believers died with Christ when he died in his body (6:3-8; Colossians 1:22). Some see a reference to the church as Christ's body, but the setting is death and resurrection.

decisions.choice: belonging to another: the marriage picture applied to Christ
decisions.reason: "To become another's" repeats the words used of the woman's second marriage in verse 3. Believers now belong to the risen Christ, as a wife to her husband (compare 2 Corinthians 11:2).

decisions.choice: bear fruit: a life that pleases God
alternatives: bear children, continuing the marriage picture
decisions.reason: The image is of fruit, the outcome of a life (6:21-22). Some hear the marriage picture continued, with offspring born to the new union, but Paul does not develop that thought.

decisions.choice: you ... we: Paul includes himself
decisions.reason: Paul turns from "you" to "we" at the end, joining himself to his readers, as he does again in verses 5-6.

decisions.choice: put to death as far as the law is concerned
decisions.reason: "Put to death to the law" means that the law no longer has any claim on them. Balanced spells out the dative so that it does not sound as if the law did the killing.

decisions.choice: When the Messiah died on the cross, you died with him ... produce good things for God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "through the body of Christ" (m2) and the fruit image (m4) with words from 6:3-8.

decisions.choice: se les dio muerte a la ley (L); se les dio muerte en lo que respecta a la ley (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is passive: something was done to them, through Christ's body (m2). "Murieron" would lose that, and "fueron muertos" is no longer natural Spanish, so Literal and Balanced use the impersonal "se les dio muerte". Readable says "murieron con él", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: mliuawa kwa habari ya sheria (L); mliuawa kwa upande wa sheria (B)
decisions.reason: "Mliuawa kwa sheria" would sound as if the law had killed them. "Kwa habari ya" / "kwa upande wa" (as regards) says that they died as far as the law is concerned, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "deveniez [ceux] d'un autre"
decisions.reason: French cannot say "become to another"; Literal supplies the pronoun in brackets so that the words match verse 3, "devient [la femme] d'un autre homme", as the Greek repeats the same expression.

decisions.choice: "열매를 맺다" at every level, here and in verse 5
decisions.reason: Bearing fruit is Paul's picture for a life that pleases God (meaning decision), set against bearing fruit for death in verse 5. Korean "열매를 맺다" is a natural and familiar picture, so it is kept at every level; Readable adds "좋은".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean (as through the letter)
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable has a deity_pronoun span, Korean says "그분" with the honorific; Korean has no capital letters for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "sinh bông trái" (L, B); "sinh ra những điều tốt đẹp" (R) (also 7:5)
decisions.reason: Bearing fruit is a life that pleases God (m4). "Sinh bông trái" keeps the picture of fruit from 6:21-22 and fits the marriage picture of verses 2-4; Readable says what the fruit is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "anh chị em" then "chúng ta"
decisions.reason: Paul includes himself in the result (m5), so the change from "you" to "we" becomes the inclusive "chúng ta", which takes in both Paul and his readers.

decisions.choice: Воскрешённому
decisions.reason: The one raised from the dead is Christ; Literal's participle stands as a title and is capitalised. Balanced and Readable say "тому, кто", lowercase like the English "the one who".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; honorific forms for Christ and God ("उनके जो ... जिलाए गए", "मसीह ... मरे")
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for God and Christ comes from the honorific third person at every level (style guide, sections 4 and 7). The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: "मसीह" with no christos setting
decisions.reason: "मसीह" is both the familiar name and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made (style guide, section 7). The same through this chapter.

source.text: ὅτε γὰρ ἦμεν ἐν τῇ σαρκί, τὰ παθήματα τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν τὰ διὰ τοῦ νόμου ἐνηργεῖτο ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ καρποφορῆσαι τῷ θανάτῳ·

records.literal_gloss: When for we were in the flesh, the passions of the sins, the [ones] through the law, were at work in the members of us for the to bear fruit to the death;

en.L: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which [came] through the law, were at work in our members to bear fruit for death;
en.B: When we lived in the flesh, the law stirred up sinful desires in us. They were at work in the parts of our bodies, and what we produced belonged to death.
en.R: Before, when our sinful selves were in control, the law only stirred up our desire to sin. Those desires were at work in our bodies, and what they produced led to death.

es.L: Porque cuando estábamos en la carne, las pasiones de los pecados, que [venían] por medio de la ley, actuaban en nuestros miembros para dar fruto para la muerte;
es.B: Cuando vivíamos en la carne, la ley despertaba en nosotros deseos pecaminosos. Actuaban en los miembros de nuestro cuerpo, y lo que producíamos pertenecía a la muerte.
es.R: Antes, cuando nuestro yo pecador nos dominaba, la ley solo despertaba en nosotros el deseo de pecar. Esos deseos actuaban en nuestro cuerpo, y lo que producían llevaba a la muerte.

sw.L: Kwa maana tulipokuwa katika mwili, tamaa za dhambi, ambazo [zilikuja] kupitia sheria, zilikuwa zikitenda kazi katika viungo vyetu ili kuzaa matunda kwa ajili ya kifo;
sw.B: Tulipotawaliwa na asili ya dhambi, sheria iliamsha ndani yetu tamaa za dhambi. Zilifanya kazi katika viungo vya miili yetu, na yale tuliyozaa yalikuwa mali ya kifo.
sw.R: Zamani, asili yetu ya dhambi ilipotutawala, sheria iliamsha tu hamu yetu ya kutenda dhambi. Tamaa hizo zilifanya kazi katika miili yetu, na matokeo yake yalituelekeza kwenye kifo.

fr.L: Car lorsque nous étions dans la chair, les passions des péchés, qui [venaient] par la Loi, agissaient dans nos membres pour porter du fruit pour la mort ;
fr.B: Quand nous vivions dans la chair, la Loi excitait en nous des passions pécheresses. Elles étaient à l’œuvre dans les parties de notre corps, et ce que nous produisions appartenait à la mort.
fr.R: Avant, quand notre nature pécheresse dirigeait notre vie, la Loi ne faisait qu’éveiller en nous l’envie de pécher. Ces envies agissaient dans notre corps, et ce qu’elles produisaient menait à la mort.

ko.L: 우리가 육신 안에 있었을 때에는, 율법으로 말미암은 죄의 정욕들이 우리 지체 안에서 작용하여 죽음에게 열매를 맺게 하였습니다.
ko.B: 우리가 육신 안에 살았을 때에는, 율법이 죄의 욕망을 일으켰고, 그 욕망이 우리 몸의 각 부분에서 활동하여 죽음을 위한 열매를 맺었습니다.
ko.R: 전에 죄에 끌리는 본성이 우리를 다스리고 있을 때에는, 율법이 오히려 죄를 짓고 싶은 마음을 부추겼습니다. 그 욕망이 우리 몸 안에서 움직였고, 그 결과는 죽음이었습니다.

vi.L: Vì khi chúng ta còn ở trong xác thịt, những đam mê của tội lỗi, là những điều [đến] qua luật pháp, đã hành động trong các chi thể của chúng ta để sinh bông trái cho sự chết;
vi.B: Khi chúng ta còn ở trong xác thịt, luật pháp đã khơi dậy những đam mê tội lỗi trong chúng ta. Chúng hoạt động trong các bộ phận của thân thể chúng ta, và những gì chúng ta sinh ra đều thuộc về sự chết.
vi.R: Trước kia, khi bản tính tội lỗi còn làm chủ chúng ta, luật pháp chỉ khơi dậy lòng ham muốn phạm tội của chúng ta. Những ham muốn ấy hoạt động trong thân thể chúng ta, và những gì chúng sinh ra đều dẫn đến sự chết.

pt.L: Pois, quando estávamos na carne, as paixões dos pecados, as [que vinham] por meio da Lei, agiam nos nossos membros para dar fruto para a morte;
pt.B: Quando vivíamos na carne, a Lei despertava em nós desejos pecaminosos. Eles agiam nas partes do nosso corpo, e o que produzíamos pertencia à morte.
pt.R: Antes, quando a nossa natureza pecadora nos controlava, a Lei só despertava em nós os desejos de pecar. Esses desejos agiam no nosso corpo, e o que produziam levava à morte.

am.L: ምክንያቱም በሥጋ በነበርን ጊዜ፣ በሕግ በኩል [የመጡት] የኃጢአት ፍትወቶች ለሞት ፍሬ እንድናፈራ በክፍሎቻችን ይሠሩ ነበር፤
am.B: በሥጋ በኖርን ጊዜ ሕጉ የኃጢአት ምኞቶችን በውስጣችን ይቀሰቅስ ነበር። እነርሱም በአካላችን ክፍሎች ይሠሩ ነበር፤ ያፈራነውም ፍሬ የሞት ነበር።
am.R: ቀድሞ ኃጢአተኛው ማንነታችን ይገዛን በነበረ ጊዜ፣ ሕጉ ኃጢአት የመሥራት ፍላጎታችንን ብቻ ቀሰቀሰ። እነዚያ ፍላጎቶች በአካላችን ውስጥ ይሠሩ ነበር፤ ያስገኙትም ውጤት ወደ ሞት መራ።

ru.L: Ведь когда мы были во плоти, страсти грехов, [возбуждаемые] Законом, действовали в наших членах, чтобы приносить плод смерти;
ru.B: Когда мы жили во плоти, Закон возбуждал в нас греховные страсти. Они действовали в частях нашего тела, и то, что мы производили, принадлежало смерти.
ru.R: Раньше, когда нами управляла греховная природа, Закон только возбуждал в нас желание грешить. Эти желания действовали в нашем теле, и то, что они производили, вело к смерти.

hi.L: क्योंकि जब हम शरीर में थे, तब पापों की वासनाएँ, जो व्यवस्था के द्वारा [उत्पन्न होती थीं], मृत्यु के लिए फल लाने को हमारे अंगों में काम करती थीं;
hi.B: जब हम शरीर में जीते थे, तब व्यवस्था ने हममें पाप की लालसाएँ भड़काईं। वे हमारी देह के अंगों में काम करती थीं, और जो फल हम लाते थे, वह मृत्यु का था।
hi.R: पहले, जब हमारा शारीरिक स्वभाव हम पर हावी था, तब व्यवस्था ने केवल हमारी पाप करने की इच्छा को भड़काया। वे इच्छाएँ हमारे शरीरों में काम करती थीं, और उनका परिणाम मृत्यु था।

uk.L: Бо коли ми були в тілі, пристрасті гріхів, [що прийшли] через Закон, діяли в наших членах, щоб приносити плід смерті;
uk.B: Коли ми жили в тілі, Закон розбурхував у нас гріховні пристрасті. Вони діяли в частинах нашого тіла, і те, що ми приносили, належало смерті.
uk.R: Раніше, коли нами керувала наша грішна природа, Закон лише розпалював у нас бажання грішити. Ці бажання діяли в нашому тілі, і те, що вони приносили, вело до смерті.

ja.L: というのは、わたしたちが肉にあったときには、律法を通して[起こる]罪の欲望が、わたしたちの肢体の中で働いて、死のために実を結ばせていたからです。
ja.B: わたしたちが肉にあって生きていたころは、律法が罪へと向かう欲望をかき立て、それがわたしたちの体の各部分の中で働いて、死のための実を結んでいました。
ja.R: 以前、罪に傾く自分の性質に支配されていたころ、律法はかえって、わたしたちの中に罪を犯したいという思いをかき立てるだけでした。そうした思いがわたしたちの体の中で働き、その結果は死へとつながっていました。

decisions.choice: in the flesh: the old life, human life under sin's sway
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" is not the body but human life in its weakness, ruled by sin and set against the Spirit. Paul speaks of it as past: in 8:9 he says believers "are not in the flesh but in the Spirit".

decisions.choice: passions of sins: passions that lead to sins
decisions.reason: The genitive describes the passions by what they produce: desires that issue in sinful deeds.

decisions.choice: through the law: the law provoked them
decisions.reason: The law did not create these passions, but its commands gave sin a way to stir them up. Paul explains how in verses 7-11, and insists that the law itself is not sin.

decisions.choice: members: the parts of the body
decisions.reason: As in 6:13 and 6:19, the members are the parts of the body through which a person acts.

decisions.choice: bear fruit for death: produce what ends in death
decisions.reason: This is the opposite of verse 4. The old life produced a harvest that belonged to death, as 6:21 says: "the end of those things is death".

decisions.choice: when our sinful selves were in control
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the flesh" means here (m1), with "sinful self" as in Romans 13:14 and Galatians 5. Literal and Balanced keep "flesh".

decisions.choice: the law stirred up sinful desires
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the law the subject of a verb to say what "passions ... through the law" means (m3). Literal brackets the verb it supplies.

decisions.choice: carne (L, B); yo pecador (R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the chapter (7:5, 18, 25). Here the flesh is human life under sin's sway (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "carne", the long-familiar Spanish way of naming that self, as the English keeps "flesh"; Readable says "yo pecador", as Galatians 5 Readable does, where the English Readable says "sinful self". In 7:14 the adjective is "carnal" (L) and "de carne" (B).

decisions.choice: mwili (L); asili ya dhambi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the chapter (7:5, 18, 25). Here the flesh is human life under sin's sway, the power set against the Spirit (m1). "Mwili" alone is the body, and "tulipoishi katika mwili" would be heard as "while we were alive in the body", so Balanced and Readable say "asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature), as Galatians 5, Romans 13:14 and Romans 8 do; Literal keeps "mwili". In 7:14 the adjective stays "wa mwili" at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: "la chair" (L, B); "notre nature pécheresse" (R) (for the whole chapter and chapter 8)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "la chair", the word Paul plays on through chapters 7-8. Readable says what it means here, human life under sin's sway, with "nature pécheresse", the plain French counterpart of the English Readable's "sinful self".

decisions.choice: "육신" (L, B); "죄에 끌리는 본성" (R) for the flesh as human nature under sin's sway, through chapters 7-8
decisions.reason: As settled for the letter, Literal says "육신"; Balanced keeps it too in chapters 7-8, where Paul sets the flesh against the Spirit and the reader needs to see the one word recur. "육체" would suggest the physical body only. Readable says what the word means here (meaning decision), "죄에 끌리는 본성", or "죄에 끌리는 나 자신" where Paul speaks of himself.

decisions.choice: "정욕" (L); "욕망" (B); "죄를 짓고 싶은 마음" (R)
decisions.reason: The noun means strong passions that lead to sins (meaning decision). "정욕" in modern Korean leans to sexual desire, so Balanced and Readable use broader words.

decisions.choice: "xác thịt" (L, B); "bản tính tội lỗi" (R) where flesh is human nature under sin's sway (through chapters 7-8)
decisions.reason: "Xác thịt" is the word kept for flesh through the letter (3:20) and in the Vietnamese Colossians. It can be heard as the body alone, so Readable says "bản tính tội lỗi" (the sinful nature), as the Vietnamese Colossians does at Readable (2:13) and as the English Readable says "sinful self" (m1).

decisions.choice: "những đam mê của tội lỗi" (L); "những đam mê tội lỗi" (B)
decisions.reason: The phrase means passions that lead to sins (m2). "Đam mê" is strong desire that carries a person along; "dục vọng" is kept for the desires of the body in 6:12.

decisions.choice: na carne (L, B); a nossa natureza pecadora (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "a carne" (docs/portuguese-style.md section 6). Readable follows the English "sinful selves" and m1, with "natureza pecadora", the plainest Portuguese for "sinful self"; 7:18 and 7:25 say the same.

decisions.choice: "ኃጢአተኛው ማንነታችን" (our sinful self) for "the flesh" at Readable
decisions.reason: In Romans 7 and 8 "flesh" is human life under sin's power. Literal and Balanced keep "ሥጋ"; Readable says what is meant, following the English Readable ("our sinful selves"), here and in 7:18, 7:25 and chapter 8 (8:3-13), as 13:14 does. "ማንነት" (who one is) is closer to the English "self" than "ተፈጥሮ" (nature); 8:3 keeps the Son's human body apart ("ሰውነቱም እንደ ኃጢአተኞች ሰዎች ሰውነት ነበር").

decisions.choice: во плоти
decisions.reason: Key term: sarx is "плоть" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "греховная природа" where the sense is moral, as the English Readable says "sinful self" (m1).

decisions.choice: "शारीरिक स्वभाव" (R); "शरीर" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Flesh (sarx) is "शरीर" at Literal and Balanced through Romans. Where it means human nature under sin's sway (meaning decision m1), Readable says "शारीरिक स्वभाव", as it will in 8:3-13; the same in 7:18 and 7:25. Where Paul means the body, Readable keeps "शरीर".

decisions.choice: "у тілі" (L, B); "наша грішна природа" (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's rendering of sarx where it is moral, the old life under sin's sway (m1): "тіло" at Literal and Balanced, with Readable saying what it means. "Плоть" is Church Slavonic in feel.

decisions.choice: "肉" (L, B); "罪に傾く自分の性質" (R) for flesh in Paul's moral sense
decisions.reason: Here flesh is human life under sin's sway, not the body (m1). Literal and Balanced keep Paul's word "肉"; Readable says what it means, as the style guide's term table asks, and uses the same phrase in 7:18 and 7:25.

decisions.choice: "欲望" (L, B) for pathēmata
decisions.reason: "情欲" today suggests sexual desire only; Paul means passions of every kind that lead to sins (m2).

source.text: νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα, ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος.

records.literal_gloss: Now but we were released from the law, having died [to that] in which we were held, so as to serve us in newness of spirit and not oldness of letter.

en.L: But now we have been released from the law, having died to that by which we were held, so that we serve in newness of [the] Spirit and not in oldness of [the] letter.
en.B: But now we are free from the law. We have died to what once held us fast, so that we serve in the new life of the Spirit, not in the old life of the written letter.
en.R: But now we are free from the law. We died, and what held us prisoner has no more power over us. So now we serve God with the new life the Spirit gives, and not in the old way of obeying written rules.

es.L: Pero ahora hemos sido liberados de la ley, habiendo muerto a aquello en que estábamos sujetos, de modo que servimos en [la] novedad del Espíritu y no en [la] vejez de la letra.
es.B: Pero ahora estamos libres de la ley. Hemos muerto a lo que antes nos tenía sujetos, de modo que servimos en la vida nueva del Espíritu, no en la vida vieja de la letra escrita.
es.R: Pero ahora estamos libres de la ley. Morimos, y lo que nos tenía presos ya no tiene poder sobre nosotros. Así que ahora servimos a Dios con la vida nueva que da el Espíritu, y no a la manera antigua de obedecer reglas escritas.

sw.L: Lakini sasa tumefunguliwa kutoka katika sheria, tukiwa tumekufa kwa kile kilichotushikilia, hata tutumikie katika upya wa Roho wala si katika ukale wa andiko.
sw.B: Lakini sasa tuko huru kutoka katika sheria. Tumekufa kwa kile kilichotushika kwa nguvu, ili tutumikie katika maisha mapya ya Roho, si katika maisha ya zamani ya sheria iliyoandikwa.
sw.R: Lakini sasa tuko huru kutoka katika sheria. Tulikufa, na kile kilichotufunga kama wafungwa hakina nguvu tena juu yetu. Kwa hiyo sasa tunamtumikia Mungu kwa uzima mpya ambao Roho anatupa, wala si kwa njia ya zamani ya kutii kanuni zilizoandikwa.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, nous avons été déliés de la Loi, étant morts à ce qui nous tenait captifs, de sorte que nous servons dans la nouveauté de [l’]Esprit et non dans l’ancienneté de [la] lettre.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, nous sommes libérés de la Loi. Nous sommes morts à ce qui nous tenait enfermés, afin de servir dans la vie nouvelle de l’Esprit, et non dans la vie ancienne de la lettre écrite.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, nous sommes libres par rapport à la Loi. Nous sommes morts, et ce qui nous tenait prisonniers n’a plus de pouvoir sur nous. Alors maintenant, nous servons Dieu avec la vie nouvelle que donne l’Esprit, et non plus à l’ancienne manière, en obéissant à des règles écrites.

ko.L: 그러나 이제 우리는 우리를 붙잡고 있던 것에 대하여 죽어서 율법에서 풀려났습니다. 그러므로 우리는 [성령의] 새로움 안에서 섬기고, 문자의 낡음 안에서 [섬기지] 않습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 이제 우리는 율법에서 풀려났습니다. 우리를 꽉 붙잡고 있던 것에 대해 우리가 죽었기 때문입니다. 그래서 우리는 기록된 율법을 따르는 옛 방식이 아니라, 성령께서 주시는 새로운 삶으로 하나님을 섬깁니다.
ko.R: 그러나 이제 우리는 율법에서 자유롭습니다. 우리는 죽었고, 우리를 가두고 있던 것은 더 이상 우리를 붙잡지 못합니다. 그래서 이제 우리는 기록된 규칙을 지키는 옛 방식이 아니라, 성령께서 주시는 새 생명으로 하나님을 섬깁니다.

vi.L: Nhưng bây giờ chúng ta đã được giải thoát khỏi luật pháp, vì đã chết đối với điều đã giam giữ chúng ta, để chúng ta phục dịch trong sự mới mẻ của Thánh Linh, chứ không trong sự cũ kỹ của văn tự.
vi.B: Nhưng nay chúng ta đã được giải thoát khỏi luật pháp. Chúng ta đã chết đối với điều từng trói buộc mình, để chúng ta phục dịch theo đời sống mới của Thánh Linh, chứ không theo lối cũ của văn tự.
vi.R: Nhưng bây giờ chúng ta đã được tự do khỏi luật pháp. Chúng ta đã chết, và điều từng giam giữ chúng ta không còn quyền gì trên chúng ta nữa. Vì vậy, bây giờ chúng ta phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời bằng đời sống mới mà Thánh Linh ban cho, chứ không theo lối cũ là vâng giữ những luật lệ thành văn.

pt.L: Mas agora fomos libertados da Lei, tendo morrido para aquilo em que estávamos presos, de modo que servimos em novidade do Espírito e não em velhice da letra.
pt.B: Mas agora estamos livres da Lei. Morremos para aquilo que antes nos prendia, e assim servimos na vida nova do Espírito, e não na vida velha da letra escrita.
pt.R: Mas agora estamos livres da Lei. Nós morremos, e aquilo que nos mantinha presos não tem mais poder sobre nós. Por isso agora servimos a Deus com a vida nova que o Espírito dá, e não do jeito antigo, obedecendo a regras escritas.

am.L: አሁን ግን ለያዘን ነገር ሞተን ከሕግ ተፈትተናል፤ ስለዚህ በፊደል አሮጌነት ሳይሆን በመንፈስ አዲስነት እናገለግላለን።
am.B: አሁን ግን ከሕግ ነጻ ነን። ቀድሞ አጥብቆ ይዞን ለነበረው ሞተናል፤ ስለዚህ በተጻፈው ፊደል አሮጌ ኑሮ ሳይሆን በመንፈስ አዲስ ሕይወት እናገለግላለን።
am.R: አሁን ግን ከሕግ ነጻ ነን። ሞተናል፤ እንደ እስረኛ ይዞን የነበረውም ከእንግዲህ በእኛ ላይ ሥልጣን የለውም። ስለዚህ አሁን የተጻፉ ደንቦችን በመጠበቅ በአሮጌው መንገድ ሳይሆን መንፈስ ቅዱስ በሚሰጠው አዲስ ሕይወት እግዚአብሔርን እናገለግላለን።

ru.L: Но теперь мы освобождены от Закона, умерев [для того], чем были удерживаемы, так что мы служим в обновлении Духа, а не в ветхости буквы.
ru.B: Но теперь мы свободны от Закона. Мы умерли для того, что когда-то держало нас, и теперь служим в новой жизни Духа, а не в старой жизни записанной буквы.
ru.R: Но теперь мы свободны от Закона. Мы умерли, и то, что держало нас в плену, больше не имеет над нами власти. Теперь мы служим Богу в новой жизни, которую даёт Дух, а не по-старому, исполняя записанные правила.

hi.L: परंतु अब हम व्यवस्था से छूट गए, क्योंकि जिसके बंधन में हम थे, उसके लिए मर गए, यहाँ तक कि हम आत्मा की नई रीति से सेवा करते हैं, न कि लेख की पुरानी रीति से।
hi.B: पर अब हम व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र हैं। हम उसके लिए मर चुके हैं जिसने हमें कभी जकड़ रखा था, ताकि हम आत्मा के नए जीवन में सेवा करें, न कि लिखे हुए अक्षर के पुराने जीवन में।
hi.R: पर अब हम व्यवस्था से स्वतंत्र हैं। हम मर गए, और जिसने हमें क़ैदी बना रखा था, उसका अब हम पर कोई अधिकार नहीं। इसलिए अब हम उस नए जीवन के साथ परमेश्वर की सेवा करते हैं जो आत्मा देता है, न कि लिखे हुए नियमों के पालन की पुरानी रीति से।

uk.L: А тепер ми звільнені від Закону, померши [для того], що нас тримало, так що ми служимо в новизні Духа, а не в старості букви.
uk.B: Але тепер ми вільні від Закону. Ми померли для того, що колись нас міцно тримало, тож служимо в новому житті Духа, а не в старому житті писаної букви.
uk.R: Але тепер ми вільні від Закону. Ми померли, і те, що тримало нас у полоні, більше не має над нами влади. Тож тепер ми служимо Богові новим життям, яке дає Дух, а не по-старому, виконуючи писані правила.

ja.L: しかし今は、わたしたちは、自分を捕らえていたものに対して死んで、律法から解かれました。それで、わたしたちは、霊の新しさにおいて仕え、文字の古さにおいてではないのです。
ja.B: しかし今は、わたしたちは律法から解き放たれています。かつてわたしたちをしっかりと捕らえていたものに対して死んだので、書かれた文字による古い生き方ではなく、霊による新しい生き方で仕えているのです。
ja.R: でも今、わたしたちは律法から自由にされています。わたしたちは死んだので、わたしたちを捕らえていたものは、もうわたしたちに何の力もありません。ですから今は、書かれた決まりを守る古いやり方ではなく、聖霊が与えてくださる新しい命によって、神に仕えているのです。

decisions.choice: that by which we were held: the law
alternatives: sin, or the old life in the flesh
decisions.reason: "Having died to that in which we were held" most naturally refers to the law just named: believers have died to it (verse 4). Some take it as sin or the old life, which also held them captive (6:6, 7:5).

decisions.choice: serve: serve as slaves serve a master
decisions.reason: douleuō is the verb of slavery. Believers still serve, but as slaves of God (6:22), in a new way.

decisions.choice: Spirit: God's Spirit
decisions.reason: Spirit and letter are set side by side as in 2:29 and 2 Corinthians 3:6, where the Spirit is God's Spirit. The word could mean the human spirit, but chapter 8 takes up the Spirit's work at length.

decisions.choice: letter: the written law
decisions.reason: gramma is what is written: the law as a code of written commands, with no power to give life (2 Corinthians 3:6). It does not mean the "literal sense" of a text.

decisions.choice: released: the law has no more claim
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 2, where the widow is released from the law of her husband.

decisions.choice: the new life of the Spirit ... the old life of the written letter
alternatives: newness of the Spirit ... oldness of the letter
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the abstract nouns "newness" and "oldness" into the life each one describes.

decisions.choice: serve God ... obeying written rules
decisions.reason: Readable names the one served (God, as in 6:22 and 7:25) and explains "letter" (m4).

decisions.choice: servimos (L, B); servimos a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a slave's service (m2), and Spanish follows the English, which says "serve" here and in 7:25 and leaves the slave picture to the meaning decision. "Servir como esclavos" (as Galatians 5:13, where the paradox is the point) would make this verse heavier than the Greek. Readable adds "a Dios", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: la letra (L); la letra escrita (B)
decisions.reason: As in 2:27-29, Literal and Balanced keep "letra", which in Spanish can stand for the written text against the Spirit (m4). Balanced adds "escrita", as the English Balanced says "written letter"; Readable says "reglas escritas".

decisions.choice: tutumikie / tunamtumikia
decisions.reason: "Kutumikia" is from the same root as "mtumwa" (slave) and "utumwa", so it keeps the slave's service of the meaning decision without adding words. Used again in 7:25.

decisions.choice: andiko (L); sheria iliyoandikwa (B); kanuni zilizoandikwa (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:27-29: "herufi" is only a letter of the alphabet. Literal says "andiko" (a writing), Balanced "sheria iliyoandikwa" (the written law, m4), and Readable "kanuni zilizoandikwa" (written rules), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "l'ancienneté"
decisions.reason: "Vieillesse" is said of people growing old. "Ancienneté" keeps the abstract noun that answers "nouveauté" and says that the letter belongs to the old order.

decisions.choice: "섬기다" for the verb at every level; "영" bracketed as "[성령의]" (L) / "성령" (B, R); "문자" (L) / "기록된 율법" (B) / "기록된 규칙" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one rendered "종노릇 하다" in 6:6, but here the master is God and the sense is service (meaning decision), so "섬기다" is used. The meaning decision reads the Spirit as God's Spirit; Literal marks that reading with "[성령의]". "문자" for the letter follows 2:27-29.

decisions.choice: "phục dịch" (L, B); "phục vụ" (R) for this verb (also 7:25; 9:12)
decisions.reason: The verb is to serve as a slave serves a master (m2). "Phục dịch" is service done under a master and keeps that edge; "phụng sự" is kept for the worship of 1:9. Readable uses the everyday "phục vụ".

decisions.choice: "Thánh Linh" and "văn tự" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Spirit is God's Spirit (m3), so it is "Thánh Linh", capitalised. The letter is the written law (m4), "văn tự" as in 2:27-29, which keeps the old contrast of Spirit and letter.

The Spirit here is God's Spirit (m3). Romans writes "霊" where the English has "the Spirit"; Readable says "聖霊", as through Romans at that level, so that a new reader does not take it as the human spirit. "御霊" is not used in this translation.

source.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν;

en.R: So what should we say about this?

es.L: ¿Qué diremos, pues?
es.B: ¿Qué hemos de decir entonces?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué debemos decir de esto?

fr.B: Que dire alors ?

ko.B: 그렇다면 우리는 무엇이라고 말해야 하겠습니까?
ko.R: 그러면 우리는 이 일에 대해 무엇이라고 말해야 하겠습니까?

ja.R: では、このことについて、わたしたちは何と言えばよいでしょうか？

decisions.choice: a question that leads to an objection
decisions.reason: Paul uses this question to raise an objection his teaching could provoke (as in 6:1 and 9:14). Verse 5 said the passions came "through the law"; does that make the law itself evil?

en.B: Is the law sin?

ru.L: Закон — грех?
ru.B: Неужели Закон — это грех?
ru.R: Значит ли это, что Закон греховен?

hi.L: क्या व्यवस्था पाप है?
hi.B: क्या व्यवस्था पाप है?
hi.R: क्या इसका अर्थ है कि व्यवस्था पापमय है?

uk.L: Закон — гріх?
uk.B: Чи Закон — це гріх?
uk.R: Чи це означає, що Закон грішний?

ja.L: 律法は罪[なのでしょう]か？
ja.B: 律法は罪なのでしょうか？
ja.R: それでは、律法そのものが罪だということでしょうか？

decisions.choice: Is the law itself sin?
decisions.reason: The objection is that if the law stirs up sinful passions (verse 5) and increases trespass (5:20), the law must be sinful. Paul rejects this at once.

decisions.choice: "율법이 나쁘다는 말입니까?" (R)
decisions.reason: "율법이 죄입니까?" would puzzle a new reader, who knows "죄" as a wrong act; Readable asks whether the law itself is bad, which is the question Paul means (meaning decision).

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔγνων εἰ μὴ διὰ νόμου, τήν τε γὰρ ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν εἰ μὴ ὁ νόμος ἔλεγεν· Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις·

records.literal_gloss: May it not be; but the sin not I knew except through law; the then for desire not I had known except the law was saying: Not you shall covet.

en.L: May it not be! Rather, I did not know sin except through [the] law; for I would not have known desire if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."
en.B: Certainly not! But it was the law that taught me what sin is. I would never have recognized wrong desire for what it is unless the law had said, "You shall not covet."
en.R: Of course not! But without the law, I would not have known what sin is. I would not have known that wanting what belongs to others is wrong if the law had not said, "Do not long for what is not yours."

es.L: ¡No sea así! Antes bien, yo no conocí el pecado sino por medio de [la] ley; pues no habría conocido el deseo si la ley no hubiera dicho: «No codiciarás».
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Pero fue la ley la que me enseñó qué es el pecado. Nunca habría reconocido el mal deseo como lo que es si la ley no hubiera dicho: «No codiciarás».
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Pero sin la ley yo no habría sabido qué es el pecado. No habría sabido que querer lo que es de otros está mal si la ley no hubiera dicho: «No desees lo que no es tuyo».

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Bali sikuijua dhambi isipokuwa kupitia sheria; kwa maana nisingeijua tamaa kama sheria isingalisema, "Usitamani."
sw.B: Hasha! Lakini ni sheria iliyonifundisha dhambi ni nini. Nisingaliweza kamwe kuitambua tamaa mbaya jinsi ilivyo kama sheria isingalisema, "Usitamani."
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Lakini bila sheria, nisingalijua dhambi ni nini. Nisingalijua kwamba kutaka vitu vya watu wengine ni kosa kama sheria isingalisema, "Usitamani kilicho cha mwingine."

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Au contraire, je n’ai connu le péché que par [la] Loi ; car je n’aurais pas connu la convoitise si la Loi n’avait dit : « Tu ne convoiteras pas. »
fr.B: Absolument pas ! Mais c’est la Loi qui m’a appris ce qu’est le péché. Je n’aurais jamais reconnu la convoitise pour ce qu’elle est si la Loi n’avait pas dit : « Tu ne convoiteras pas. »
fr.R: Pas du tout ! Mais sans la Loi, je n’aurais pas su ce qu’est le péché. Je n’aurais pas su que c’est mal d’avoir envie de ce qui appartient aux autres, si la Loi n’avait pas dit : « Ne désire pas ce qui n’est pas à toi. »

ko.L: 결코 그럴 수 없습니다! 오히려 나는 율법을 통하지 않고서는 죄를 알지 못했습니다. 율법이 "탐내지 말라" 하고 말하지 않았다면, 나는 탐심을 알지 못했을 것입니다.
ko.B: 절대로 그렇지 않습니다! 오히려 율법이 아니었다면 나는 죄가 무엇인지 알지 못했을 것입니다. 율법이 "탐내지 말라" 하고 말하지 않았다면, 나는 탐내는 마음이 무엇인지 몰랐을 것입니다.
ko.R: 절대 아닙니다! 그러나 율법이 없었다면, 나는 죄가 무엇인지 몰랐을 것입니다. 율법이 "남의 것을 갖고 싶어 하지 말라" 하고 말하지 않았다면, 남의 것을 갖고 싶어 하는 것이 잘못이라는 것을 나는 몰랐을 것입니다.

vi.L: Không hề như vậy! Nhưng tôi đã không biết tội lỗi nếu không qua luật pháp; vì tôi đã không biết sự tham muốn nếu luật pháp không nói: "Ngươi chớ tham muốn."
vi.B: Chẳng hề như vậy! Nhưng chính luật pháp đã cho tôi biết tội lỗi là gì. Tôi sẽ không bao giờ nhận ra lòng tham muốn sai trái là gì nếu luật pháp không nói: "Ngươi không được tham muốn."
vi.R: Không đời nào! Nhưng nếu không có luật pháp, tôi đã không biết tội lỗi là gì. Tôi đã không biết rằng ham muốn những gì thuộc về người khác là sai, nếu luật pháp không nói: "Đừng thèm muốn những gì không phải của mình."

pt.L: Que não aconteça! Pelo contrário, eu não conheci o pecado senão por meio da Lei; pois eu não teria conhecido o desejo se a Lei não dissesse: "Não cobiçarás."
pt.B: De forma alguma! Mas foi a Lei que me ensinou o que é o pecado. Eu nunca teria reconhecido o mau desejo como ele é, se a Lei não tivesse dito: "Não cobiçarás."
pt.R: Claro que não! Mas, sem a Lei, eu não saberia o que é o pecado. Eu não saberia que é errado querer o que é dos outros, se a Lei não tivesse dito: "Não desejes o que não é teu."

am.L: ከቶ አይሁን! ነገር ግን በሕግ በኩል ካልሆነ በቀር ኃጢአትን አላወቅኩም፤ ሕጉ «አትመኝ» ባይል ኖሮ ምኞትን አላውቅም ነበርና።
am.B: በፍጹም! ነገር ግን ኃጢአት ምን እንደ ሆነ ያስተማረኝ ሕጉ ነው። ሕጉ «አትመኝ» ባይል ኖሮ ክፉ ምኞትን ምን እንደ ሆነ ፈጽሞ ባልተረዳኩ ነበር።
am.R: በጭራሽ! ነገር ግን ሕጉ ባይኖር ኖሮ ኃጢአት ምን እንደ ሆነ ባላወቅኩ ነበር። ሕጉ «የአንተ ያልሆነውን አትመኝ» ባይል ኖሮ የሌሎችን ነገር መፈለግ ስሕተት እንደ ሆነ ባላወቅኩ ነበር።

ru.L: Да не будет! Но я не познал греха иначе как через Закон; ведь я не знал бы и пожелания, если бы Закон не говорил: «Не будешь желать.»
ru.B: Ни в коем случае! Но именно Закон научил меня, что такое грех. Я бы никогда не распознал дурное желание, если бы Закон не сказал: «Не желай чужого.»
ru.R: Конечно, нет! Но без Закона я не знал бы, что такое грех. Я не знал бы, что плохо хотеть чужого, если бы Закон не сказал: «Не желай того, что принадлежит другому.»

hi.L: ऐसा कभी न हो! वरन् व्यवस्था के बिना मैं पाप को नहीं पहचानता; क्योंकि मैं लालसा को न जानता, यदि व्यवस्था यह न कहती, "तुम लालच नहीं करोगे।"
hi.B: कदापि नहीं! पर व्यवस्था ने ही मुझे सिखाया कि पाप क्या है। मैं बुरी लालसा को कभी उसके असली रूप में न पहचानता, यदि व्यवस्था यह न कहती, "लालच मत करो।"
hi.R: बिलकुल नहीं! पर व्यवस्था के बिना मैं न जानता कि पाप क्या है। मैं न जानता कि दूसरों की चीज़ें पाने की चाह ग़लत है, यदि व्यवस्था यह न कहती, "जो तुम्हारा नहीं है, उसकी लालसा मत करो।"

uk.L: Нехай не буде! Але я не пізнав гріха інакше, як через Закон; бо я не знав би пожадливості, якби Закон не казав: «Не пожадай.»
uk.B: Аж ніяк! Але саме Закон навчив мене, що таке гріх. Я ніколи не розпізнав би лихого бажання, якби Закон не сказав: «Не пожадай.»
uk.R: Звичайно, ні! Але без Закону я не знав би, що таке гріх. Я не знав би, що хотіти чужого — погано, якби Закон не сказав: «Не бажай того, що не твоє.»

ja.L: 決してそうではありません！むしろ、わたしは律法によらなければ罪を知りませんでした。実際、律法が「むさぼってはならない」と言わなかったなら、わたしはむさぼりを知らなかったでしょう。
ja.B: 決してそうではありません！むしろ、罪とは何かをわたしに教えたのは律法でした。もし律法が「むさぼってはならない」と言わなかったなら、わたしはむさぼりをそれと見分けることはなかったでしょう。
ja.R: そんなことはありません！けれども、律法がなければ、わたしは罪が何かを知らなかったでしょう。もし律法が「人のものを欲しがってはならない」と言わなかったなら、人のものを欲しがることが悪いとは知らなかったでしょう。

decisions.choice: "I" in 7:7-25: a speaker whose identity is debated; the text keeps "I"
decisions.reason: From here to the end of the chapter Paul speaks as "I". Who this "I" is has long been debated. He may be telling his own story as a Jew who met the law's command; or speaking as Adam, who received the first command, was deceived and died (verses 9-11 echo Genesis 2-3); or as Israel, which received the law at Sinai; or as anyone who lives under the law without the Spirit, a figure of speech in which a writer says "I" to draw the reader in. In verses 14-25 a further question arises (see 7:14). The text is translated with "I" at every level, so that readers can weigh the question themselves.

decisions.choice: Exodus 20:17 and Deuteronomy 5:21
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the tenth commandment from the Greek Old Testament, but only its first words, without the list of a neighbor's house, wife and goods. Shortened like this, it forbids wrong desire as such.

decisions.choice: desire: craving for what God has forbidden
decisions.reason: epithymia and the verb in the commandment share a root. The word can mean any strong desire; here it is the desire the commandment forbids, the root of other sins.

decisions.choice: I did not know ... I would not have known: knowing sin as sin
decisions.reason: The first verb says that the law is how the speaker came to know sin; the second, with the condition that follows, says what would have been true without the law. Knowing here is recognition: the law shows sin for what it is (3:20).

decisions.choice: Certainly not! (B); Of course not! (R)
decisions.reason: The same rendering as in 3:4, 3:31 and 9:14. Literal keeps "May it not be!"

decisions.choice: wanting what belongs to others ... Do not long for what is not yours
decisions.reason: "Covet" is not an everyday word, so Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: ¡No sea así! (L); ¡De ningún modo! (B); ¡Claro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:4 and 11:1, the same Spanish is used at each level wherever Romans has Paul's strongest no: here and in 7:13.

decisions.choice: yo, first person (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The "I" of 7:7-25 is kept as "I" at every level, as the English keeps it (m1). Spanish shows the person in the verb, and adds "yo" where the Greek has the pronoun or where the speaker needs to stay in view (7:7, 9, 14, 17, 20, 25), so the reader is not led to settle who is speaking.

decisions.choice: querer lo que es de otros ... «No desees lo que no es tuyo»
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "codiciarás", the commandment as Spanish readers know it. Readable says what coveting is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Isiwe hivyo! (L); Hasha! (B); Sivyo kabisa! (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:4 and 11:1, the same Swahili is used at each level wherever Romans has Paul's strongest no: here and in 7:13.

decisions.choice: tamaa; Usitamani
decisions.reason: "Tamaa" and "kutamani" are one root in Swahili as the Greek noun and verb are, so the link between the desire and the commandment can be heard. The "I" of 7:7-25 is kept as "I" at every level (m1); Swahili adds the free pronoun "mimi" where the Greek has its pronoun (7:9, 14, 17, 20, 25).

decisions.choice: "la convoitise", "Tu ne convoiteras pas" (L, B)
decisions.reason: French "convoiter" and "convoitise" share a root, as the Greek noun and verb do, and say the desire the commandment forbids. Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "결코 그럴 수 없습니다!" (L); "절대로 그렇지 않습니다!" (B); "절대 아닙니다!" (R), as settled at 3:4
decisions.reason: The same fixed form for each level as through the letter.

decisions.choice: "나" in 7:7-25 with 합쇼체 ("나는 ... 알지 못했습니다"); the commandment in 해라체 ("탐내지 말라")
decisions.reason: Paul keeps writing to the readers in the 합쇼체 of the letter, so the speaking "I" is the plain "나" used through the letter; the meaning decision leaves open who this "I" is, and the Korean keeps "나" without deciding. The commandment is Scripture and stays in 해라체, as settled at 2:24.

decisions.choice: "sự tham muốn" and "Ngươi chớ tham muốn" (L); "lòng tham muốn sai trái" and "Ngươi không được tham muốn" (B)
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb of the commandment are one Greek word (m3), so Vietnamese uses "tham muốn" for both, and the reader hears that the law named the very desire. The commandment speaks with "ngươi", as the commandments are quoted in the Vietnamese Matthew (4:7, 4:10).

decisions.choice: "tôi" for the speaker of 7:7-25
decisions.reason: The meaning decision keeps "I" and leaves open who is meant, with a footnote. "Tôi" is Paul's word for himself through the letter, so it keeps the same openness without choosing.

decisions.choice: Não cobiçarás (L, B); Não desejes o que não é teu (R)
decisions.reason: The commandment keeps God's "tu" at every level (docs/portuguese-style.md section 4): the future "cobiçarás" in Literal and Balanced, the plain negative command in Readable, which also explains "cobiçar" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ምኞት" (desire) and "አትመኝ" (do not desire, covet)
decisions.reason: The noun "desire" and the commandment "you shall not covet" are the same Greek word; the Amharic noun and verb from one root keep that link, which the argument depends on.

decisions.choice: пожелание; «Не будешь желать» (L); желание; «Не желай чужого» (B)
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb share a root, as in Greek (m3), and the commandment has the wording of 13:9 and of the commandments in Matthew 19:18. "Возжелай" is Slavonic; Readable says what coveting is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: я
decisions.reason: The "I" of 7:7-25 is kept as "я" at every level, without a setting: the speaker is not God or Christ (m1).

decisions.choice: "ऐसा कभी न हो!" (L); "कदापि नहीं!" (B); "बिलकुल नहीं!" (R)
decisions.reason: Paul's strong denial, the same form at each level as in chapters 3 and 6 and through Romans. The same in 7:13.

decisions.choice: the quoted commandment moves to the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: Hindi puts the condition after the main clause here so that the sentence can end with the commandment, as the English does, and its full stop stays inside the quotation.

decisions.choice: "むさぼり" / "むさぼってはならない" (L, B); "人のものを欲しがる" (R)
alternatives: "欲望" for the noun and "むさぼる" for the verb
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb of the commandment share a root in the Greek (m3). Japanese keeps the link by using the same word for both, "むさぼり" and "むさぼる", and again in 7:8. The commandment is Scripture, so it is in the plain style.

decisions.choice: "わたし" for the speaker of 7:7-25 at every level
decisions.reason: Who the "I" is remains open (m1). Japanese keeps the first person "わたし" all through, as the Greek does, so that no level decides the question.

source.text: ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς κατειργάσατο ἐν ἐμοὶ πᾶσαν ἐπιθυμίαν, χωρὶς γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία νεκρά.

records.literal_gloss: An opening but having taken the sin through the commandment produced in me every desire; apart from for law sin [is] dead.

en.L: But sin, having found an opening through the commandment, worked in me every desire; for apart from [the] law sin [is] dead.
en.B: Sin found its opening in the commandment and used it to rouse every kind of wrong desire in me, for without the law sin is dead.
en.R: But sin used the command as a chance to attack. Through the command, sin made me want all kinds of wrong things. Without the law, sin has no power.
