decisions.reason: Here the word is a rule or pattern the speaker finds at work (m1), not the Law of Moses, so it is not capitalised; so too the "other law" and the "law of sin" in 7:23 and 7:25. "Закон Божий" keeps the capital.

decisions.choice: "नियम" (B, R) for the law Paul finds at work, and for the law of sin (7:23, 7:25); "व्यवस्था" (L)
decisions.reason: Here law means a rule or pattern at work in the self (meaning decision m1), not the law of Moses. Literal keeps "व्यवस्था" so the play on the one Greek word stays visible; Balanced and Readable say "नियम", keeping "व्यवस्था" for God's law.

decisions.choice: "закон", lowercase, in 7:21-25 for a ruling power; "Закон Божий" capitalised
decisions.reason: The style guide writes "закон" for a rule or ruling power the speaker finds at work (m1; "інший закон", "закон гріха", "закон мого розуму") and "Закон" for God's law, so the reader can see which is meant in Paul's play on the word.

decisions.choice: "律法" (L); "法則" (B, R) for nomos as a rule that always holds
decisions.reason: Here nomos seems to mean a pattern that always holds (m1), as in 3:27 and 8:2. Literal keeps "律法" so the reader sees Paul's play on the one word through 7:21-25; Balanced and Readable say "法則", a rule at work. "神の律法" stays "律法" at every level.

source.text: συνήδομαι γὰρ τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον, βλέπω δὲ ἕτερον νόμον ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου ἀντιστρατευόμενον τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ νοός μου καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντά με ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τῷ ὄντι ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου.

records.literal_gloss: I delight with for in the law of the God according to the inner man, \v 23 I see but another law in the members of me warring against the law of the mind of me and taking captive me in the law of the sin, the [one] being in the members of me.

en.L: For I delight in the law of God according to the inner person, \v 23 but I see another law in my members warring against the law of my mind and taking me prisoner by the law of sin, which is in my members.
en.B: In my inner self I gladly agree with God's law. \v 23 But I see another law in the parts of my body. It is at war with the law of my mind, and it takes me prisoner to the law of sin that is in those parts of my body.
en.R: Deep inside, I love God's law. \v 23 But I see another power at work in my body. It fights against what my mind knows is right. It makes me a prisoner of sin, which is at work in my body.

es.L: Porque me deleito en la ley de Dios según el ser interior, \v 23 pero veo otra ley en mis miembros que hace guerra contra la ley de mi mente y me lleva cautivo por la ley del pecado que está en mis miembros.
es.B: En mi ser interior acepto con gozo la ley de Dios. \v 23 Pero veo otra ley en los miembros de mi cuerpo. Está en guerra con la ley de mi mente, y me hace prisionero de la ley del pecado que está en los miembros de mi cuerpo.
es.R: En lo más profundo de mí, amo la ley de Dios. \v 23 Pero veo otro poder que actúa en mi cuerpo. Lucha contra lo que mi mente sabe que es correcto. Me hace prisionero del pecado, que actúa en mi cuerpo.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninafurahishwa na sheria ya Mungu kwa kadiri ya utu wa ndani, \v 23 lakini ninaona katika viungo vyangu sheria nyingine inayofanya vita dhidi ya sheria ya akili yangu na kunichukua mateka kwa sheria ya dhambi, ile iliyomo katika viungo vyangu.
sw.B: Katika utu wangu wa ndani ninakubaliana kwa furaha na sheria ya Mungu. \v 23 Lakini ninaona sheria nyingine katika viungo vya mwili wangu. Inapigana vita na sheria ya akili yangu, na inanichukua mateka kwa sheria ya dhambi iliyomo katika viungo hivyo vya mwili wangu.
sw.R: Ndani kabisa ya moyo wangu, ninaipenda sheria ya Mungu. \v 23 Lakini ninaona nguvu nyingine ikifanya kazi katika mwili wangu. Inapigana na kile ambacho akili yangu inajua kuwa ni sahihi. Inanifanya mfungwa wa dhambi, ambayo inafanya kazi katika mwili wangu.

fr.L: Car je prends plaisir à la Loi de Dieu selon {{gender:l’être intérieur|l’homme intérieur}}, \v 23 mais je vois dans mes membres une autre loi qui combat contre la loi de ma raison et qui me rend prisonnier par la loi du péché qui est dans mes membres.
fr.B: Dans mon être intérieur, j’approuve avec joie la Loi de Dieu. \v 23 Mais je vois dans les parties de mon corps une autre loi. Elle fait la guerre à la loi de ma raison, et elle me fait prisonnier de la loi du péché qui est dans les parties de mon corps.
fr.R: Au fond de moi, j’aime la Loi de Dieu. \v 23 Mais je vois une autre force à l’œuvre dans mon corps. Elle se bat contre ce que ma raison sait être juste. Elle me rend prisonnier du péché, qui agit dans mon corps.

ko.L: 나는 속사람으로는 하나님의 율법을 즐거워하지만, \v 23 내 지체 안에서 다른 법이 내 마음의 법과 싸워, 내 지체 안에 있는 죄의 법으로 나를 사로잡는 것을 봅니다.
ko.B: 내 속사람은 하나님의 율법을 기뻐합니다. \v 23 그러나 내 몸의 각 부분에서 다른 법이 활동하는 것을 봅니다. 그 법은 내 마음의 법과 싸워서, 내 몸 안에 있는 죄의 법에 나를 포로로 사로잡습니다.
ko.R: 나는 마음속 깊이 하나님의 율법을 사랑합니다. \v 23 그러나 내 몸 안에서 다른 힘이 움직이는 것을 봅니다. 그 힘은 내 마음이 옳다고 아는 것과 맞서 싸웁니다. 그리고 내 몸 안에서 움직이는 죄의 포로가 되게 합니다.

vi.L: Vì theo con người bề trong, tôi vui thích luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời, \v 23 nhưng tôi thấy một luật khác trong các chi thể của tôi, chiến đấu chống lại luật của tâm trí tôi, và bắt tôi làm tù binh trong luật của tội lỗi, là [luật] ở trong các chi thể của tôi.
vi.B: Trong con người bề trong, tôi vui lòng đồng ý với luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 23 Nhưng tôi thấy một luật khác trong các bộ phận của thân thể tôi. Luật ấy chiến đấu chống lại luật của tâm trí tôi, và bắt tôi làm tù binh cho luật của tội lỗi đang ở trong các bộ phận của thân thể tôi.
vi.R: Tận đáy lòng, tôi yêu thích luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 23 Nhưng tôi thấy một quyền lực khác đang hoạt động trong thân thể tôi. Nó chiến đấu chống lại điều mà tâm trí tôi biết là đúng. Nó biến tôi thành tù binh của tội lỗi, là quyền lực đang hoạt động trong thân thể tôi.

pt.L: Pois tenho prazer na Lei de Deus segundo o ser interior, \v 23 mas vejo outra lei nos meus membros, guerreando contra a lei da minha mente e me fazendo prisioneiro pela lei do pecado, que está nos meus membros.
pt.B: No meu íntimo, concordo com alegria com a Lei de Deus. \v 23 Mas vejo outra lei nas partes do meu corpo. Ela está em guerra contra a lei da minha mente e me faz prisioneiro da lei do pecado, que está nessas partes do meu corpo.
pt.R: Bem lá no fundo, eu amo a Lei de Deus. \v 23 Mas vejo outro poder agindo no meu corpo. Ele luta contra o que a minha mente sabe que é certo. Ele me faz prisioneiro do pecado, que age no meu corpo.

am.L: እንደ ውስጣዊው ሰው በእግዚአብሔር ሕግ ደስ ይለኛልና፤ \v 23 ነገር ግን በክፍሎቼ ውስጥ ሌላ ሕግ የአእምሮዬን ሕግ ሲዋጋና በክፍሎቼ ውስጥ ባለው በኃጢአት ሕግ ሲማርከኝ አያለሁ።
am.B: በውስጣዊ ማንነቴ በእግዚአብሔር ሕግ በደስታ እስማማለሁ። \v 23 ነገር ግን በአካሌ ክፍሎች ውስጥ ሌላ ሕግ አያለሁ። እርሱ ከአእምሮዬ ሕግ ጋር ይዋጋል፤ በአካሌ ክፍሎች ውስጥ ላለው የኃጢአት ሕግም እስረኛ አድርጎ ይወስደኛል።
am.R: በልቤ ጥልቅ የእግዚአብሔርን ሕግ እወዳለሁ። \v 23 ነገር ግን በአካሌ ውስጥ የሚሠራ ሌላ ኃይል አያለሁ። አእምሮዬ ትክክል እንደ ሆነ የሚያውቀውን ይዋጋል። በአካሌ ውስጥ የሚሠራው የኃጢአት እስረኛ ያደርገኛል።

ru.L: Ведь я с радостью согласен с Законом Бога по внутреннему человеку, \v 23 но вижу другой закон в моих членах, воюющий против закона моего ума и берущий меня в плен законом греха, находящимся в моих членах.
ru.B: В глубине души я с радостью соглашаюсь с Законом Бога. \v 23 Но в частях моего тела я вижу другой закон. Он воюет против закона моего ума и берёт меня в плен закону греха, который в частях моего тела.
ru.R: В глубине души я люблю Закон Бога. \v 23 Но я вижу, что в моём теле действует другая сила. Она борется с тем, что мой ум признаёт правильным. Она делает меня пленником греха, который действует в моём теле.

hi.L: क्योंकि मैं भीतरी मनुष्यत्व के अनुसार परमेश्वर की व्यवस्था से प्रसन्न रहता हूँ, \v 23 परंतु मुझे अपने अंगों में दूसरी व्यवस्था दिखाई देती है, जो मेरी बुद्धि की व्यवस्था से लड़ती है, और मुझे पाप की उस व्यवस्था का बंदी बनाती है जो मेरे अंगों में है।
hi.B: अपने भीतरी मन में मैं परमेश्वर की व्यवस्था से ख़ुशी से सहमत हूँ। \v 23 पर मैं अपनी देह के अंगों में एक दूसरा नियम देखता हूँ। वह मेरी बुद्धि की व्यवस्था से युद्ध करता है, और मुझे पाप के उस नियम का बंदी बना लेता है जो मेरी देह के अंगों में है।
hi.R: भीतर से मैं परमेश्वर की व्यवस्था से प्रेम करता हूँ। \v 23 पर मैं अपने शरीर में एक और शक्ति को काम करते देखता हूँ। वह उस बात के विरुद्ध लड़ती है जिसे मेरी बुद्धि सही जानती है। वह मुझे पाप का बंदी बना देती है, जो मेरे शरीर में काम करता है।

uk.L: Бо я радію Законові Божому за внутрішньою людиною, \v 23 але бачу інший закон у моїх членах, що воює проти закону мого розуму й бере мене в полон законом гріха, що в моїх членах.
uk.B: У своєму внутрішньому єстві я радо погоджуюся з Божим Законом. \v 23 Але в частинах свого тіла я бачу інший закон. Він воює проти закону мого розуму і бере мене в полон до закону гріха, що в частинах мого тіла.
uk.R: Глибоко в душі я люблю Божий Закон. \v 23 Але я бачу, що в моєму тілі діє інша сила. Вона бореться проти того, що мій розум визнає правильним. Вона робить мене бранцем гріха, який діє в моєму тілі.

ja.L: わたしは、内なる人によれば、神の律法を喜んでいるからです。\v 23 しかし、わたしの肢体の中には別の律法があって、わたしの理性の律法に対して戦いを挑み、わたしの肢体の中にある罪の律法のうちに、わたしを捕虜にしているのを、わたしは見ます。
ja.B: 内なる自分としては、わたしは神の律法を喜んで受け入れています。\v 23 しかし、わたしの体の各部分には別の法則があるのが見えます。それはわたしの理性の法則と戦い、体の各部分にある罪の法則のもとに、わたしを捕虜として連れて行くのです。
ja.R: 心の奥では、わたしは神の律法を愛しています。\v 23 しかし、わたしの体の中では、別の力が働いているのが見えます。その力は、わたしの心が正しいと知っていることと戦い、わたしを罪の捕虜にしてしまいます。罪はわたしの体の中で働いているのです。

decisions.choice: the inner person: the self that thinks and wills
alternatives: the new self created by the Spirit
decisions.reason: The inner person is the mind and will, as opposed to the outward life of the body (2 Corinthians 4:16). Some see here the new self that God creates (Ephesians 3:16), which would make the speaker a believer; the phrase itself does not settle that question (see 7:14).

decisions.choice: delight in: rejoice in, gladly agree with
decisions.reason: synēdomai is to take pleasure in something along with others. The speaker's inner self is glad of God's law.

decisions.choice: another law, the law of sin: a ruling power
decisions.reason: "Law" is stretched to mean a power that rules and commands. The "law of sin" is sin's rule, which works through the body and is set against God's law. Paul plays on the word, as in verse 21 and 8:2.

decisions.choice: the law of my mind: God's law as the mind acknowledges it
alternatives: a principle of reason in the mind
decisions.reason: The law of the mind is most likely God's law (verse 22), which the mind approves and serves (verse 25). Some take it as the mind's own rule, a principle of reason.

decisions.choice: warring ... taking prisoner: a military picture
decisions.reason: The other law fights a campaign against the mind and carries the speaker off as a prisoner of war.

decisions.choice: by the law of sin: sin's law holds the prisoner
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "to" or "by": the speaker is made captive to the law of sin, or by means of it. Either way, sin's rule holds him.

decisions.choice: inner person (L); inner self (B); Deep inside (R)
decisions.reason: The inner person is the speaker himself, so no gender setting is used. "Person" is the human word, which fits a speaker who may stand for others.

decisions.choice: another power ... what my mind knows is right ... a prisoner of sin
decisions.reason: Readable explains each use of "law" by what it means (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: el ser interior (L); mi ser interior (B); en lo más profundo de mí (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase names the self that thinks and wills (m1), not a man as against a woman. The familiar "el hombre interior" would read as male to many readers, so Spanish says "ser interior", as the English says "inner person" and "inner self"; Readable follows the English "Deep inside".

decisions.choice: utu wa ndani (L); utu wangu wa ndani (B); ndani kabisa ya moyo wangu (R)
decisions.reason: "Utu wa ndani" (inner humanness) is the natural Swahili phrase for the inner self (m1) and is not male, so no setting is needed; Readable follows the English "Deep inside".

decisions.choice: {{gender:l'être intérieur|l'homme intérieur}} (L)
decisions.reason: The English "inner person" needs no setting, but the traditional French phrase uses "homme"; the default says "l'être intérieur", which fits a speaker who may stand for others, and keeps the traditional phrase as the alternative. Balanced and Readable say "mon être intérieur" and "au fond de moi", which need none.

decisions.choice: "ma raison"
decisions.reason: "Esprit" would be confused with the Spirit of God in 7:6 and chapter 8. "Raison" is the mind that thinks and judges, which agrees with God's law.

decisions.choice: "속사람" (L, B); "마음속 깊이" (R); "마음" for the mind
decisions.reason: "속사람" is the Korean word for the inner person, the self that thinks and wills (meaning decision); Readable says it plainly. "마음" for "mind" fits Korean, where the mind that knows and the heart are one word.

decisions.choice: "다른 힘" and "죄의 포로" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "another law" and "the law of sin" as a ruling power. Readable says "힘", as the English Readable says "power", so the new reader does not take it for another written law.

decisions.choice: "con người bề trong" (L, B); "tận đáy lòng" (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase is the self that thinks and wills (m1). "Con người bề trong" keeps the Greek "inner person"; Readable uses the everyday idiom "deep in the heart", as the English says "Deep inside".

decisions.choice: o ser interior (L); no meu íntimo (B)
decisions.reason: As the English "inner person": "ser interior" names the self that thinks and wills (m1) without "homem", and needs no gender setting. Balanced says it the Portuguese way, "no meu íntimo".

decisions.choice: "ውስጣዊው ሰው" (L); "ውስጣዊ ማንነቴ" (my inner self, B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "inner person"; Balanced uses the current Amharic word for the self. Readable says "deep in my heart" ("በልቤ ጥልቅ").

decisions.choice: по внутреннему человеку
decisions.reason: The inner person is the speaker himself, and "человек" is already inclusive, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: "理性" (L, B) for nous; "心" (R)
decisions.reason: nous is the mind that thinks and approves (m4), set against the flesh in 7:25. "理性" names that faculty; Readable uses the everyday "心".

decisions.choice: "別の律法", "罪の律法" (L); "別の法則", "罪の法則" (B)
decisions.reason: As in 7:21: these laws are ruling powers (m3), not the law of Moses. Literal keeps the one word "律法"; Balanced uses "法則" so that "神の律法" stands out against them.

decisions.choice: wretched: miserable, worn down by distress
decisions.reason: talaipōros describes someone in great misery (compare Revelation 3:17). It is a cry of despair, not a confession of a single sin.

decisions.choice: this: the body ruled by death that has just been described
alternatives: this death, the death described in verses 9-13
decisions.reason: "This" may go with "death" (the death of verses 9-13) or with the whole phrase ("this body of death"). The sense comes to the same: the body, through which sin's law works (verse 23), is bound over to death.

decisions.choice: body of death: bodily life under the power of sin and death
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls "the body of sin" in 6:6. Rescue comes in 8:10-11 and 8:23, where God gives life to mortal bodies and redeems them.

decisions.choice: Who will rescue me?: a cry for a rescuer
decisions.reason: The future tense looks for someone to come to the rescue. The answer follows in verse 25 and in chapter 8.

decisions.choice: man, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: anthrōpos here is the speaker himself, so the word is not given the inclusive setting used where people in general are meant.

decisions.choice: the body of this death (L); this body of death (B)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Greek order and Balanced the more natural one; both carry the sense in m2.

decisions.choice: ¡Hombre desdichado [que] soy yo! (L); ¡Qué hombre tan desdichado soy! (B); ¡Pobre de mí! (R)
decisions.reason: "Hombre" here is Paul himself (r-en-1), so it takes no gender setting. Literal and Balanced keep it and say "desdichado" (wretched, worn down by distress, m1); Readable says "¡Pobre de mí!", the everyday Spanish cry of misery, where the English Readable says "How miserable I am!". The wording is drafted to stay clear of the familiar Reina-Valera line.

decisions.choice: Mimi mtu mnyonge! (L); Mimi ni mtu mnyonge kama nini! (B); Nina taabu kubwa mno! (R)
decisions.reason: "Mtu" is Paul himself and is not male, so no setting. "Mnyonge" is one who is wretched and helpless (m1); Readable says "Nina taabu kubwa mno!" (my distress is very great), as the English Readable loosens the cry. The wording keeps clear of the familiar Union Version line.

decisions.choice: mwili wa kifo hiki (L); mwili huu wa kifo (B)
decisions.reason: As in the English: Literal follows the Greek, where "this" goes with "death"; Balanced puts it with "body" (m2).

decisions.choice: "Misérable que je suis" (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the natural French cry, which needs no word for "man"; Literal keeps "homme", with no gender setting, since the speaker is speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" is already inclusive, so the English "man" without a setting needs no span in Korean.

decisions.choice: "この死の体" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Japanese "この死の体" can be read as "this body of death" or "the body of this death", which keeps the open question of what "this" goes with (m2) at both levels.

hi.B: हमारे प्रभु यीशु मसीह के द्वारा परमेश्वर का धन्यवाद हो!

ja.R: わたしたちの主イエス・{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}によってわたしを救い出してくださる神に、感謝します！

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude given to God
decisions.reason: charis with "to God" and no verb is the set phrase for giving thanks, as in 6:17 and 2 Corinthians 8:16 and 9:15.

decisions.choice: Thanks be to God
alternatives: the grace of God [will rescue me]
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "thanks to God". Some manuscripts read "I thank God", and others "the grace of God" (as if answering the question: the grace of God will rescue me). The meaning is much the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: through Jesus Christ: the answer to verse 24
decisions.reason: The thanksgiving answers the cry of verse 24 in short: God rescues through Jesus Christ. Chapter 8 spells this out.

decisions.choice: Thanks (L, B); I thank (R)
decisions.reason: The key term is rendered "thanks" here because the sense is gratitude (m1), as in 2 Corinthians 8:16 and 9:15.

decisions.choice: who rescues me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the thanks are for, picking up "rescue" from verse 24 (m3).

decisions.choice: Gracias (L, B); Doy gracias (R)
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "gracia" here means thanks (m1). Spanish "gracias" comes from the same root, so the link is kept without changing the sense. Literal brackets the verb the Greek leaves out; Readable says "Doy gracias", as the English Readable says "I thank".

decisions.choice: Shukrani [ziwe] (L); Mungu ashukuriwe (B); Ninamshukuru Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "neema" (grace) here means thanks (m1), so Swahili says "shukrani" / "kushukuru". Readable says "Ninamshukuru" (I thank), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Благодарение
decisions.reason: The Greek word is charis, the key term for grace, but here the sense is thanks (m1), so Russian says "благодарение", which shares its root with "благодать".

am.L: እንግዲያስ እኔ ራሴ በአእምሮ ለእግዚአብሔር ሕግ እገዛለሁ፤ በሥጋ ግን ለኃጢአት ሕግ [እገዛለሁ]።

ru.L: Итак, я сам умом служу Закону Бога, а плотью — закону греха.
ru.B: Итак, я сам умом служу Закону Бога, а плотью — закону греха.
ru.R: Вот где я нахожусь. Умом я служу Закону Бога. А моя греховная природа служит закону греха.

hi.L: इसलिए मैं स्वयं बुद्धि से तो परमेश्वर की व्यवस्था की, परंतु शरीर से पाप की व्यवस्था की सेवा करता हूँ।
hi.B: इसलिए मैं स्वयं अपनी बुद्धि से परमेश्वर की व्यवस्था की सेवा करता हूँ, पर अपने शरीर से पाप के नियम की।

uk.L: Тож я сам розумом служу Законові Божому, а тілом — законові гріха.
uk.B: Отже, я сам розумом служу Божому Законові, а тілом — законові гріха.
uk.R: Тож ось у якому я становищі. Розумом я служу Божому Законові. А моя грішна природа служить законові гріха.

ja.L: こういうわけで、わたし自身は、理性では神の律法に、しかし肉では罪の律法に仕えているのです。
ja.B: ですから、わたし自身は、理性では神の律法に、肉では罪の法則に仕えているのです。
ja.R: これが今のわたしの姿です。心では神の律法に仕えています。しかし、罪に傾くわたしの性質は、罪の法則に仕えているのです。

decisions.choice: I myself: the same person in both halves
alternatives: I left to myself, apart from Christ
decisions.reason: autos egō is emphatic: one and the same "I" serves both laws. Some take it as "I left to myself", that is, apart from Christ's help, which would make the sentence a summary of verses 14-24 before chapter 8 brings the answer; others see the believer's ongoing state, after the thanksgiving (see 7:14).

decisions.choice: serve: serve as a slave
decisions.reason: douleuō is the verb of slavery, as in verse 6. The speaker is a slave to two masters at once.

decisions.choice: mind ... flesh: the willing self and the self ruled by sin
decisions.reason: The mind is the inner person of verse 22, which agrees with God's law. The flesh is the self under sin's power (verses 14, 18).

decisions.choice: my sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m3), as in 7:5 and 7:18.

decisions.choice: serves the law of sin
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood in the second half. Readable repeats it; Literal and Balanced leave it understood.

decisions.choice: ninaitumikia
decisions.reason: As in 7:6, "kutumikia" (from the root of "mtumwa", slave) keeps the slave's service of m2. Flesh is "mwili" at Literal and "asili ya dhambi" at Balanced and Readable, as settled in 7:5.

decisions.choice: "섬기다" at every level for the verb of serving as a slave
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Literal renders "종노릇 하다" when the master is sin in 6:6. Here one object is God's law, so "섬기다" is used for both halves, keeping them parallel as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: one verb "仕えている" at the end for both halves (L, B)
alternatives: repeating the verb in each half
decisions.reason: The Greek says "serve" once and leaves it understood in the second half. Japanese puts the verb last, so a single "仕えている" after both halves keeps the Greek's shape without brackets; Readable repeats it, as the English Readable does.
